title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; previous bounds like Landauer's limit are insufficient for realistic finite-time processes.
method: Applies fluctuation-dissipation theorems and linear response theory to model computation as a stochastic thermodynamic process, deriving trade-offs between speed, accuracy, and energy dissipation.
result: Establishes optimal efficiency bounds for irreversible computing operations, showing that minimal dissipation scales with the square of the change in logical entropy and inversely with process duration.
conclusion: Provides a unified thermodynamic framework for optimal computation, guiding the design of energy-efficient information processors.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, achieving coherent control and readout of the nuclear spin qubit.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times and high control fidelities, but coupling them to quantum dots is challenging. This work aims to integrate a nuclear spin qubit with a quantum dot platform for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors use a silicon quantum dot device with a 73Ge atom implanted near the dot. They employ spin-dependent tunneling and radio-frequency reflectometry to initialize, control, and read out the nuclear spin state.
result: They demonstrate coherent Rabi oscillations and Ramsey fringes of the 73Ge nuclear spin, with coherence times exceeding 100 microseconds, and achieve single-shot readout fidelity above 90%.
conclusion: This work establishes a new hybrid platform combining a group-IV nuclear spin with a quantum dot, opening the door to long-lived qubits and quantum memories in silicon-based quantum processors.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using a catalyst that is returned unchanged, can enhance state transformations under local operations and classical communication (LOCC), and characterizes the catalytic power in terms of entanglement measures.
motivation: Understanding the limits of entanglement manipulation under LOCC is fundamental to quantum information theory. Catalysis can enable transformations that are otherwise impossible, but its interplay with classical communication was not fully understood.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC transformations, introducing the concept of catalytic majorization and using entanglement monotones to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for catalytic convertibility.
result: They prove that catalysis can overcome previously known restrictions, and provide a complete characterization of when a state can be catalytically converted to another under LOCC, linking it to the existence of a suitable catalyst.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis significantly expands the set of achievable LOCC transformations, and the conditions derived offer a practical tool for identifying catalytic advantages in entanglement manipulation.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: To improve quantum memory performance by leveraging complementary advantages of GEM and EIT protocols.
method: Experimental demonstration of a hybrid memory that uses GEM for time-to-frequency conversion and EIT for frequency-to-time conversion.
result: Successful reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence with enhanced efficiency and bandwidth.
conclusion: The hybrid approach offers a versatile platform for quantum networking applications.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series data using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: To learn thermodynamic properties (e.g., entropy production, free energy) from experimental time-series without prior knowledge of the underlying dynamics.
method: The authors use information-theoretic measures (correlation currents and trajectory-fluctuation currents) derived from observed trajectories to infer thermodynamic quantities.
result: They demonstrate that these currents can be used to reconstruct the thermodynamic structure of small systems, including entropy production and detailed balance violations.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical framework for extracting thermodynamic information from complex systems where direct measurement of forces or energies is infeasible.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond the conventional decomposition of entropy production.
method: Uses geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to define housekeeping and excess information flows.
result: Derives a decomposition that separates information flow into a part maintaining steady-state correlations and a part driving transient changes.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in autonomous systems, linking information flow to thermodynamic efficiency.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI-QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI-QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with a focus on entanglement swapping and purification to extend distance.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI-QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI-QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical secure quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: This work provides a consistent thermodynamic description for quantum systems where measurement context matters, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions whether time is fundamental or emergent; this work aims to demonstrate that time can be defined internally via entropy exchange.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different sectors (e.g., motional and internal degrees of freedom) is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, showing that time can emerge from thermodynamic correlations.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time may be an emergent property arising from entropy exchange, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link losses, detector performance, and finite-size effects to model achievable key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, yielding secure key rates orders of magnitude higher than existing systems.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite-to-ground QKD is a promising path to practical global quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing that many phenomena previously considered classical have hidden quantum properties.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in the boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, and to uncover quantum resources that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum and classical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness and identifies new quantum features in processes previously thought to be classical.
conclusion: The work provides a clearer demarcation of quantumness in individual processes, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust, reconfigurable entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that dissipative entanglement can be made reconfigurable, allowing generation of various multipartite entangled states, and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing and topological state preparation.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation in hybrid spin-cavity systems provides a scalable and robust platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the unprotected system, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD faces challenges in achieving high secret key rates with discrete modulation while maintaining rigorous security proofs. The authors aim to bridge this gap.
method: They combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with an improved security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and composable security framework.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can be both high-rate and provably secure, bringing practical quantum networks closer to deployment.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives under continuous monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime can scale exponentially with system size under certain measurement rates, providing a strategy to protect fragile quantum data.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to exponentially extend quantum information lifetime, offering a practical approach to improve quantum memory and computation.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip implementing self-testing quantum random number expansion, a core device-independent protocol.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale self-testing quantum random number generators for practical security applications.
method: Integrates all photonic components (source, measurement, control) on a silicon chip and performs a self-testing protocol that certifies randomness without trusting the devices.
result: Achieves high-speed random number generation with provable security based on Bell inequality violation, all on a compact chip.
conclusion: This work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices using self-testing protocols.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource-efficient and loss-tolerant quantum communications.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware. The authors aim to improve efficiency and feasibility.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation of quantum tree-codes and introduce asymmetric code geometries that are optimized for specific loss and noise parameters, using numerical simulations to evaluate performance.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce resource requirements (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates and tolerance to photon loss.
conclusion: The hierarchical design and asymmetric optimization make tree-code-based quantum repeaters more practical for near-term experimental implementations, advancing the goal of scalable quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform that combines long coherence times with high-fidelity readout, overcoming limitations of existing systems like NV centers.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for quantum information processing.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or tomography) with the entropy accumulation theorem to produce composable security bounds that are tighter than worst-case analysis.
result: The framework yields security proofs that account for device imperfections while maintaining rigorous composable security, enabling more efficient and practical QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device characterization, facilitating standards and certification for QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by turning dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error detection and fault tolerance in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: Achieving simultaneously high-fidelity gates and readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but crosstalk and calibration challenges often limit performance.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and introduce a novel calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations in a fixed-frequency transmon qubit architecture.
result: They report single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.92%, two-qubit gate fidelity of 99.91%, and readout fidelity of 99.93% on the same device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that all essential operations for quantum computation can be performed with ultra-high fidelity in a single superconducting platform, advancing the path toward fault-tolerant quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, deriving the spectral density and the threshold for decodability under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the threshold determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to generate pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for practical quantum computing and cryptography.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum resource theories, specifically magic state resource theory, and information-theoretic arguments to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required.
result: They show that to achieve a given level of pseudorandomness, the number of T gates must scale at least linearly with the number of qubits, and provide explicit bounds.
conclusion: Extensive doping with non-Clifford gates is necessary for pseudorandomness, which has implications for the design of efficient quantum circuits and the security of quantum cryptographic protocols.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing but lack a unified stabilizer framework. The authors aim to develop such a formalism to enable error correction and fault-tolerant operations.
method: The authors generalize the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over a ring, defining hybrid stabilizer states and codes.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes, and show that these codes can improve displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a foundation for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation in hybrid oscillator-qudit processors, with potential applications in sensing.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly to the thermal state.
result: The local circuit approach maintains rapid mixing and accuracy while being significantly more feasible for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum thermodynamics and simulation on current hardware.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from mesoscopic to macroscopic.

title: Entanglement Improving Coordination In Distributed Systems
authors: Francisco Ferreira Da Silva And Stephanie Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Ferreira da Silva and Stephanie Wehner

Coordination in distributed systems is often hampered by communication latency, which degrades performance. Quantum entanglement offers fundamentally stronger correlations than classically achievable without communication. Crucially, these correlations manifest instantaneously upon measurement, irre…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062611] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement can improve coordination in distributed systems by reducing the impact of communication latency.
motivation: Coordination in distributed systems is limited by communication latency; quantum entanglement offers stronger-than-classical correlations that could mitigate this.
method: The authors analyze a distributed coordination task where parties share entanglement and compare performance with classical-only protocols, using information-theoretic measures.
result: Entanglement enables better coordination than any classical protocol without communication, and can reduce the amount of communication needed to achieve a given coordination level.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement provides a genuine advantage for distributed coordination, with implications for distributed computing and communication protocols.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient biochemical and quantum devices.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating entropy production to the coherence number of the oscillation.
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and provide a rigorous proof of the dissipation-coherence tradeoff, showing that higher coherence requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental thermodynamic constraint on autonomous oscillations, with implications for both classical and quantum systems.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved, with explicit bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified thermodynamic bound that constrains the performance of thermoelectric engines, relevant for optimizing quantum thermal machines.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits as quantum error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and that the code properties are stable under partial measurements.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing and for characterizing the information-theoretic properties of monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze random Clifford circuits with interspersed measurements, treating the measurement outcomes as syndrome information. They derive conditions for decodability and compute logical error rates using statistical mechanics mappings.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that the code exhibits a transition from a decodable to an undecodable phase as measurement rate increases. The logical measurement statistics reveal a stability property under partial measurements.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum circuits can be viewed as quantum error-correcting codes with measurement-assisted decoding, providing new insights into the role of measurements in quantum information processing.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits of Gaussian cooling were unknown; non-Gaussian resources may overcome these limits.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling using covariance matrix formalism and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can achieve lower temperatures.
result: Gaussian cooling is bounded by a simple inequality; non-Gaussian resources can surpass this bound, enabling sub-bath cooling.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a practical advantage for cooling bosonic systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Unraveling system-bath dynamics into quantum trajectories reveals an entanglement transition from volume-law to area-law scaling as measurement strength increases.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement behaves in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors study a unitary system-bath model and analyze the entanglement entropy of quantum trajectories under continuous monitoring.
result: They observe a sharp transition in the scaling of entanglement entropy as a function of measurement strength, reminiscent of measurement-induced phase transitions.
conclusion: The entanglement transition in unitary system-bath dynamics provides a new perspective on the interplay between unitary evolution and dissipation, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity single-qutrit gates using coherent control on a superconducting transmon, achieving fidelities above 99.9%.
motivation: Qutrits offer a larger Hilbert space for quantum computation, but implementing high-fidelity single-qutrit gates is challenging due to leakage and control constraints.
method: Uses a superconducting transmon qutrit with coherent control via microwave pulses, employing derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) and optimal control to suppress leakage.
result: Achieves single-qutrit gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% with gate times around 20 ns, demonstrated via randomized benchmarking and process tomography.
conclusion: Coherent control enables efficient, high-fidelity single-qutrit gates, paving the way for qutrit-based quantum processors.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and many-body physics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a lower bound on nonlocal magic.
result: They find a 'magic barrier' where the magic resource initially grows, then decays before thermalization, indicating a nontrivial dynamical behavior.
conclusion: The magic barrier provides insight into the interplay between entanglement and nonstabilizerness during thermalization, with implications for quantum resource theories.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel, i.e., the ability to send information backward in time through a noisy closed timelike curve.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication through closed timelike curves (CTCs) is of theoretical interest in quantum information theory and may shed light on the nature of causality and quantum mechanics.
method: The authors model a noisy postselected CTC as a quantum channel and derive the retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic tools, including entanglement-assisted and unassisted scenarios.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity for various noise models, showing that it can be nonzero even in the presence of noise, and provide explicit formulas.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous framework for retrocausal communication and reveals that quantum channels can support backward-in-time information transfer under certain conditions.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, using a mechanical mode as one arm to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: SU(1,1) interferometers offer sub-shot-noise sensitivity and robustness to losses, but implementations are typically all-optical. Integrating a mechanical mode could enable new sensing capabilities and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors design a hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer where one arm is a mechanical mode, using two-mode squeezing and optomechanical coupling to generate entanglement and enhance phase sensitivity.
result: The hybrid interferometer achieves sub-shot-noise sensitivity and shows robustness to detection losses, with potential for improved performance over all-optical versions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable hybrid quantum system combining optomechanics and quantum interferometry, opening avenues for precision sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons via photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors lack speed and continuous operation.
method: The detector uses a superconducting island coupled to a microwave resonator; a photon triggers quasiparticle tunneling, producing a measurable current pulse.
result: Demonstrates fast, continuous, and efficient detection of individual propagating microwave photons with low dark counts.
conclusion: This detector could enable practical applications in quantum information and dark matter detection, bridging a gap in microwave photon sensing.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem to simulate noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem in quantum Monte Carlo; an efficient algorithm is needed to study open quantum system dynamics.
method: The algorithm uses population dynamics to stochastically compress and evolve the density matrix, continuously suppressing the sign problem during real-time evolution.
result: The method enables accurate simulation of open quantum system dynamics with reduced computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for simulating noisy quantum circuits, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Pound-Drever-Hall readout method for superconducting qubits, enabling ultrastable and scalable parallel readout.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high stability and low noise.
method: The authors adapt the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall technique, originally used in optics, to the microwave domain for superconducting-qubit readout.
result: The PDH method provides ultrastable readout with reduced sensitivity to fluctuations, enabling parallel readout of many qubits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical path toward scalable superconducting-qubit readout, crucial for large-scale quantum processors.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Predicts anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by exciton-phonon coupling and temperature.
motivation: To understand and predict collective emission phenomena in molecular aggregates coupled to polaritonic cavities, which are relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
method: Develops a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polariton formation, solving the dynamics to compute emission rates.
result: Finds that superradiance can be thermally activated, counterintuitively enhanced by stronger exciton-phonon coupling and higher temperatures, unlike free-space behavior.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling collective emission in polaritonic systems, with potential applications in quantum optics and energy transfer.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Understanding the boundary between quantum and classical behavior is a central problem in quantum information. The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability representation offers a framework to characterize nonclassicality.
method: The authors analyze the set of experiments (POVMs and states) that yield positive KD distributions, using measure-theoretic arguments to show that this set has measure zero in the space of all experiments.
result: They prove that the set of experiments with classical KD representations is almost surely minimal, meaning that almost all experiments are nonclassical in this sense.
conclusion: This result provides a rigorous characterization of the quantum-classical boundary within the KD framework, highlighting the prevalence of nonclassicality in quantum experiments.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations, providing rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems is challenging due to infinite Hilbert spaces; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors formulate a hierarchy of semidefinite programs (SDPs) based on moment relaxations, yielding converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values.
result: The method produces rigorous, robust bounds for observables in the stationary state, demonstrated on examples like the damped harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and rigorous way to characterize stationary states of bosonic open systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum optics.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources have correlated intensity drifts that leak information and break standard decoy-state assumptions, so tighter security bounds are needed.
method: The authors formulate the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations and solves it numerically.
result: They obtain tighter asymptotic key rates compared to previous analyses that assumed independent intensities.
conclusion: The nonlinear programming approach provides more realistic and secure key rates for practical decoy-state QKD systems.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type quantum measurements and operations, applying the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and energy conservation constraints to derive trade-off relations between accuracy and disturbance.
result: They obtain quantitative bounds on the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations under energy conservation, showing that perfect accuracy is impossible when the measured observable does not commute with the Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that must be considered in designing high-precision quantum experiments and quantum information processing tasks.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding using collective dressed states in Rydberg-blockaded atomic arrays, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: To realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit, leveraging the nonlinearity of a multilevel Rydberg superatom.
method: Uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms, mapping the system to the Jaynes-Cummings model to encode qudits in collective dressed states.
result: Demonstrates that the system can perform arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit, with potential for high-fidelity quantum control.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a scalable approach to qudit-based quantum information processing in Rydberg atom arrays.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture under dissipation, relevant to quantum transport and hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding photon-mediated energy transfer in engineered quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a donor ring coupled to a central acceptor driven by a single quantized photon mode, using a Lindblad master equation with spontaneous loss and pure dephasing.
result: They find that the photon mode mediates hybridization between donor and acceptor states, and that dissipative transport can be controlled by cavity parameters.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a tunable platform for studying quantum transport and may have applications in quantum networks and energy transfer.

title: Capacity-time Trade-off In Highly Reliable Quantum Memory
authors: Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), And C. P. Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), and C. P. Sun (孙昌璞)

Reliable quantum storage in practice relies on precise calibration of key parameters, notably the global detuning, while inevitably being subject to the combined influence of multiple disorder sources. In this work, a comprehensive model for an electromagnetically induced transparency protocol is co…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062613] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a comprehensive model for electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in quantum memory, revealing a trade-off between storage capacity and operation time under disorder.
motivation: Reliable quantum storage requires precise calibration of parameters like global detuning, but disorder from multiple sources degrades performance. The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits imposed by disorder.
method: They construct a model for an EIT-based quantum memory, incorporating various disorder sources (e.g., inhomogeneous broadening) and analyzing the storage fidelity as a function of capacity and time.
result: A capacity-time trade-off is derived: higher storage capacity (more modes) reduces the achievable storage time for a given fidelity threshold, and vice versa.
conclusion: The trade-off provides a design principle for optimizing quantum memories, balancing storage capacity and coherence time in the presence of disorder.

title: Chiral Dark Mode For Nonreciprocal Transmission And Asymmetric Quantum State Transfer In A Magneto-optical Hybrid System
authors: Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, And Xin-You Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, and Xin-You Lü

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity. Through magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, we establish a chiral optomagnonic coupling which leads to a dark mode occurring only under one …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063718] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system using magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, enabling asymmetric quantum state transfer.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer, which are important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The system couples a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity via magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, creating chiral optomagnonic coupling that yields a dark mode under one direction of propagation.
result: The chiral dark mode enables nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer between the two cavities.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal devices and quantum state transfer in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows how to concentrate it into a single qubit, providing operational protocols and bounds.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry under a continuous symmetry group, is a key quantum resource but lacks systematic concentration methods. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: The paper formalizes unspeakable coherence as a resource theory using asymmetry measures and develops protocols for concentrating coherence from multiple copies into a single system, leveraging tools from quantum resource theories.
result: They derive optimal conversion rates and demonstrate that concentration is possible with vanishing error in the asymptotic limit, with explicit protocols for qubit systems.
conclusion: Unspeakable coherence can be efficiently concentrated, establishing it as a useful resource for quantum information tasks.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the necessity of entanglement.
motivation: Quantum teleportation traditionally requires entanglement; this work explores whether path superposition can replace entanglement, potentially reducing resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender and receiver share a separable state but the sender's path is superposed, enabling perfect teleportation of a qubit.
result: Perfect teleportation fidelity is achieved with separable states when path superposition is employed, demonstrating a new resource for teleportation.
conclusion: Path superposition can serve as an alternative resource to entanglement for quantum teleportation, broadening the understanding of quantum communication resources.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Reference-frame-independent Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Over Asymmetric Channels
authors: Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, And Kejin Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, and Kejin Wei

Reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (RFI-MDI-QKD) offers a promising approach for building star-type quantum secure networks, removing the need for reference frame alignment and eliminating all detector side channel attacks. While prior experiments con…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063715] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent QKD over asymmetric channels, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: To remove the need for reference frame alignment and eliminate detector side-channel attacks in QKD, enabling robust star-type quantum networks.
method: Implemented RFI-MDI-QKD protocol over asymmetric channels with experimental setup, analyzing key rate and error tolerance.
result: Achieved secure key distribution over asymmetric channels without active reference frame alignment, demonstrating feasibility for real-world networks.
conclusion: RFI-MDI-QKD is a practical solution for building secure quantum networks with asymmetric links, reducing system complexity.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri

Designing a miniature microscale engine that can override the role of thermal fluctuations has remained elusive and is an important open challenge. Here, we provide the design and theoretical framework for a unique information-based engine—a work-to-work converter—comprising a submicron-sized bead a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064407] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for a miniature work-to-work converter engine powered by motor proteins, operating as an information-based engine at the microscale.
motivation: Designing a microscale engine that can override thermal fluctuations is an open challenge; this work aims to provide a design and theoretical framework for such an engine.
method: The authors propose a submicron-sized bead and motor protein system as a work-to-work converter, using information-based engine principles.
result: The paper presents a theoretical framework for a miniature engine that converts work from one form to another, leveraging information to overcome thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The proposed design offers a viable path to creating microscale engines that can operate effectively in the presence of thermal noise, with potential applications in nanotechnology.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) system, demonstrating a new platform for ICO beyond photonic systems.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information processing, but most experiments have been limited to photonic platforms. Exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications and insights.
method: The authors propose a cavity QED setup with two cavities and analyze the conditions for realizing ICO using the quantum switch, modeling the interaction with atoms and cavities.
result: They show that ICO can be achieved in cavity QED with high fidelity under realistic parameters, and discuss the effects of decoherence and cavity losses.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, potentially enabling integration with other quantum technologies and advancing quantum information processing.
