title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but efficient methods are lacking for many systems.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, then use classical sampling to prepare the Gibbs state.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial-depth circuits, achieving efficient sampling at finite temperature.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for Gibbs state preparation in topological systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and error correction.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple physical systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: To understand how early life could harvest energy without complex molecular machinery, by exploiting cyclic environmental changes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system coupled to a cyclic environment, analyzing energy extraction via non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
result: They show that cyclic environments can drive chemical reactions to produce high-energy molecules, providing a robust energy harvesting mechanism.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental fluctuations can serve as a simple, general source of chemical power, offering insights into prebiotic energy transduction.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on the information that can be extracted from neural activity via MEG, constrained by both quantum sensing bounds and biological energy budgets.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit from quantum metrology to magnetic field sensing, and couples it with the metabolic power available to neural currents to compute an upper bound on the information capacity.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets an upper bound on the number of distinguishable magnetic field patterns per unit time, linking quantum sensing limits to biological constraints.
conclusion: The information capacity of MEG is fundamentally limited by both quantum mechanics and metabolism, providing a theoretical benchmark for sensor development and interpretation of neural signals.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is important for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: Rephrases entanglement-depth certification as a likelihood-based model using neural quantum states trained on randomized Pauli measurement data.
result: Demonstrates that the method can certify entanglement depth and non-separability with high accuracy and scalability.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a practical and scalable tool for entanglement-depth certification from limited measurement data.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise can cause systematic errors in randomized benchmarking, leading to inaccurate gate fidelity estimates.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real quantum devices often exhibit correlated noise, which can bias fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the RB decay under temporally correlated noise and perform numerical simulations to quantify the bias.
result: They show that temporal correlations can lead to significant over- or under-estimation of average gate fidelity, and propose a modified protocol to mitigate these errors.
conclusion: Temporal correlations are a blind spot for standard RB, and accounting for them is crucial for reliable characterization of quantum gates.

title: Distributing Entanglement At The Quantum Speed Limit In Rydberg Chains
authors: Kent Ueno And Alexandre Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Kent Ueno and Alexandre Cooper

We numerically study the transport of Rydberg excitations in chains of neutral atoms. We realize an effective flip-flop interaction using off-resonant driving fields. By tuning the relative distances between atoms and applying atom-selective detuning fields, we fulfill the perfect transport conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023260] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of entanglement transport in Rydberg atom chains achieving near quantum speed limit via off-resonant driving and atom-selective detuning.
motivation: To understand and optimize the distribution of entanglement in neutral atom chains, which is crucial for quantum networking and quantum information processing.
method: Numerical simulation of Rydberg excitation transport using an effective flip-flop interaction realized by off-resonant driving fields, with tunable interatomic distances and detuning to satisfy perfect transport conditions.
result: The protocol achieves entanglement transport at the quantum speed limit, with high fidelity and minimal decoherence.
conclusion: Rydberg atom chains can serve as efficient quantum channels for distributing entanglement, with potential applications in quantum networks and quantum computing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis states are used for robust entangled differential phase sensing, offering common-mode noise rejection for quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise; entangled states can enhance sensitivity but are fragile.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic insensitivity to common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase sensing while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments by leveraging the noise-rejection properties of Lieb-Mattis states.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with engineered spin-motion coupling and coherent control to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms for quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local nondestructive readout and coherent manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These findings provide insights into qubit leakage and inform the design of more robust readout protocols for superconducting qubits.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit platforms.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts induced by ionizing radiation in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, using state-of-the-art radiation protection.
result: They identify a new type of correlated error—phase error bursts—that occur even with radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase errors from ionizing radiation pose a significant challenge for scalable quantum computing, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduced model that preserves relevant dynamics for given measurement observables is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure in time that adapts to the measurement channel's time resolution, projecting the full dynamics onto a reduced subspace that reproduces the measurement outcomes.
result: The method is demonstrated on a quantum thermal machine and a driven dissipative system, showing accurate reproduction of observables with significantly fewer degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining provides an efficient and principled way to reduce model complexity in open quantum systems while retaining predictive power for measured quantities.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The method accurately identifies the number and parameters of spin baths in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient and scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays stabilize exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded superradiance and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms, analyzing the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg arrays provides a platform for realizing kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated on neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress non-adiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic driving, enabling systematic construction of control Hamiltonians.
result: The new method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale quantum processors, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods for spatially correlated noise scale poorly with system size.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise models, improving error suppression efficiency.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for multi-qubit systems with correlated noise.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is challenging.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical system, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a cavity-mode multiplexing technique to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms. Scaling to many atoms requires parallel processing.
method: The authors introduce mode multiplexing using a single optical cavity with multiple spatial modes, each addressing a different atom, and demonstrate parallel cavity-enhanced operations.
result: They show that cavity-mode multiplexing allows simultaneous high-fidelity operations on multiple atoms, significantly increasing the processing speed and scalability of neutral-atom arrays.
conclusion: This technique paves the way for large-scale neutral-atom quantum computers with fast cavity-mediated interactions.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive; reducing the simulation overhead is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps to achieve lower error scaling with fewer gates.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution provides a practical and efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation for phase estimation, making quantum chemistry simulations more feasible on near-term devices.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement and non-equilibrium dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to study string-breaking dynamics under adiabatic and diabatic conditions.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics beyond simple breaking, including oscillatory and multi-string behavior.
conclusion: The work provides new probes of string breaking and demonstrates that confining strings can display complex quantum dynamics, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems (qudits) often suffer from demolition errors and long readout times, limiting their use in quantum information processing. The authors aim to enhance the nondemolition nature of measurements to preserve quantum states for subsequent operations.
method: The protocol uses adaptive subspace-switching readout, where the measurement basis is dynamically adjusted based on prior outcomes to minimize disturbance. This is implemented on a silicon quantum dot platform with spin qudits.
result: The adaptive readout achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% and reduces measurement-induced errors, outperforming standard readout schemes. The method is demonstrated across multiple qudit levels and is platform-agnostic.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly improves the nondemolition character of quantum measurements, enabling higher-fidelity state preparation and more efficient quantum error correction in multilevel systems.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is critical for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when simulating variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm development.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors degrade qubit performance; protecting idle operation without active error correction is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons in a triangular geometry to be equal, opening a gap between computational and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This approach offers a simple, hardware-efficient method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding and detecting quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing many-body systems, but existing methods often require full state tomography or are limited to specific settings.
method: The authors propose using repeated interventions (process tensors) to construct projected ensembles that capture the chaotic dynamics, leveraging tools from open quantum systems and quantum information.
result: They show that the projected ensemble approach can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provides a unified framework for various chaos diagnostics, such as out-of-time-ordered correlators and spectral statistics.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and scalable way to probe quantum chaos in experiments, with potential applications in quantum simulation and thermalization studies.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving parity dynamics essential for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast and noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems to resolve parity states and enable Kitaev chain qubits.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They achieve fast readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout technique for Majorana-based qubits, advancing the development of topological quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental implementations (CV-QKD, entanglement distribution, quantum networks).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates and long-distance demonstrations, including satellite-based links.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in loss tolerance and security proofs.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predictive computational methods can guide the design of better qubits.
method: The paper reviews ab initio cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for systems with strong higher-order contributions or surface-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the development of solid-state spin qubits for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as standard quantum theory and classical gravity are incompatible; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the information-theoretic constraints and experimental feasibility.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising near-term avenue.

title: Adaptable Route To Fast Coherent State Transport Via Bang-Bang-Bang Protocols
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, and H. H. Jen

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an adaptable bang-bang-bang protocol for fast coherent state transport of atomic qubits, achieving high fidelity with reduced time.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow, limiting efficient quantum operations; fast transport is needed for scalable quantum computation.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence with three instantaneous pulses to steer the atomic state along a desired path, optimized via numerical methods.
result: Demonstrates high-fidelity transport in a fraction of the adiabatic time, with robustness to parameter variations.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, fast, and adaptable method for coherent state transport in atomic quantum systems.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a one-axis-twisting echo control method to enhance collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles, improving metrological gain.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom suffer from limited squeezing due to decoherence and complexity. The authors aim to develop a simpler and more robust method to boost squeezing.
method: They introduce a one-axis-twisting echo control sequence applied to individual atoms within an ensemble, which refocuses unwanted evolution and enhances the squeezing interaction.
result: The proposed scheme achieves significantly higher squeezing levels compared to standard one-axis-twisting, with improved resilience to inhomogeneous broadening and other noise sources.
conclusion: The echo control technique provides a practical and effective way to generate strong spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, advancing quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how measurement imaginarity (a resource in the resource theory of imaginarity) can enhance entanglement concentration in bipartite quantum states.
motivation: Imaginarity has been recognized as a quantum resource, and its operational role in entanglement manipulation is not fully understood. The authors aim to explore whether using measurements with imaginary components can improve the efficiency of entanglement concentration.
method: The authors analyze the entanglement concentration protocol using local operations and classical communication (LOCC) and compare the success probability when measurements are restricted to real-valued versus complex-valued (imaginarity-containing) operations. They derive conditions and bounds for the advantage.
result: They show that measurements with non-zero imaginarity can increase the success probability of entanglement concentration for certain quantum states, demonstrating a clear operational advantage of imaginarity as a resource.
conclusion: Imaginarity in measurements can be a useful resource for entanglement manipulation, suggesting that complex numbers play a non-trivial operational role in quantum information processing.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To extend the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems and demonstrate its universal intrinsic contribution, which is robust against parameter fluctuations.
method: Trapped ion platform used to simulate higher-rank spin tensors and measure the Hall effect under controlled conditions.
result: Observed universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The trapped ion system provides a versatile platform for studying higher-rank spin transport phenomena, with potential applications in spintronics and quantum simulation.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics system to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then leverages dissipative dynamics to generate bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates that n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be generated and tuned by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Separable Squeezed States In Finite-memory Structured Reservoir
authors: Austen Couvertier And Ting Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Austen Couvertier and Ting Yu

Entanglement in continuous-variable Gaussian systems is a key resource, and common reservoirs can both suppress and generate correlations. Existing work focused on preentangled states or Markovian baths, leaving open whether separable squeezed inputs entangle in structured environments or under modu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063724] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement generation from separable squeezed states in a finite-memory structured reservoir, extending beyond Markovian baths.
motivation: Understanding how structured environments can generate entanglement from initially separable states is important for quantum information processing with continuous-variable systems.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of two squeezed states coupled to a common non-Markovian reservoir with finite memory, using exact master equations.
result: They find that entanglement can be generated from separable squeezed inputs under certain conditions, and the reservoir memory and squeezing parameters play crucial roles.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs can be exploited to create entanglement from separable states, offering new possibilities for quantum information tasks.

title: Beyond Qubits: Multilevel Quantum Sensing For Dark Matter
authors: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, And Ernst David Herbschleb
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, and Ernst David Herbschleb

Searching for ultralight dark matter requires detecting extremely weak oscillating fields, where quantum sensing is especially promising. The authors show that spin-1 nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond can harness multilevel quantum states to combine enhanced signal response with common mode noise suppression, improving sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060802] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: NV centers in diamond are used as multilevel quantum sensors to detect ultralight dark matter, improving sensitivity via common-mode noise suppression.
motivation: Ultralight dark matter detection requires extremely sensitive quantum sensors; NV centers offer a promising platform.
method: The authors propose using spin-1 NV centers with multilevel quantum states to enhance signal response while suppressing common-mode noise.
result: The multilevel approach improves sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions compared to conventional two-level sensing.
conclusion: Multilevel quantum sensing with NV centers is a viable and improved method for dark matter detection.

title: Nonadiabatic Self-healing Of Trotter Errors In Digitized Counterdiabatic Dynamics
authors: Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, And Koushik Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, and Koushik Paul

Trotter errors in digitized quantum dynamics arise from approximating time-ordered evolution under noncommuting Hamiltonian terms with a product formula. In the adiabatic regime, such errors are known to exhibit long-time self-healing [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that Trotter errors in digitized counterdiabatic dynamics can self-heal nonadiabatically, improving the fidelity of quantum simulations.
motivation: Trotter errors limit the accuracy of digital quantum simulation; understanding and mitigating them is crucial for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze digitized counterdiabatic dynamics using a product formula and derive conditions under which Trotter errors self-heal even outside the adiabatic regime.
result: They show that nonadiabatic self-healing occurs, leading to reduced error accumulation and higher fidelity compared to standard Trotterization.
conclusion: Digitized counterdiabatic protocols can exploit self-healing to achieve more accurate quantum simulations with fewer Trotter steps.

title: Oh Molecule As A Quantum Probe To Jointly Estimate Electric And Magnetic Fields
authors: Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, And Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, and Matteo G. A. Paris

The hydroxyl radical (the OH molecule) carries both electric and magnetic dipole moments and, as a diatomic molecule, admits a comparatively simple and accurate model. This makes it a natural quantum probe for the joint estimation of electric and magnetic fields. Here we study simultaneous estimatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062612] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The OH molecule is proposed as a quantum probe for simultaneous estimation of electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: Joint estimation of multiple fields is important for sensing, and the OH molecule's dual dipole moments make it a natural candidate.
method: The authors model the OH molecule as a quantum system and analyze simultaneous estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: They find that simultaneous estimation can outperform separate estimation due to correlations, and provide bounds on achievable precision.
conclusion: The OH molecule is a viable platform for multi-parameter quantum sensing, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a simpler, more accessible approach without sacrificing accuracy.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the use of standard master equation techniques while capturing non-Markovian effects.
result: The method yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, significantly reducing computational complexity compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian master equations more practical for studying open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that restrict dynamic range; existing methods trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this using weak measurements and entanglement.
method: The protocol employs sequential weak measurements on coherent spin states, where ancilla qubits are weakly entangled with the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian estimation is used to track the frequency.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, effectively extending the dynamic range.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements with ancilla entanglement provide a practical route to high-precision, wide-dynamic-range quantum frequency estimation, relevant for quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which is essential for understanding fluctuations and thermodynamics in non-equilibrium systems.
method: The authors construct a stochastic calculus for Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and showing how they reduce to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that bridges jump and diffusion processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across different stochastic regimes.
conclusion: This work provides a foundational tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics, with potential applications to fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic bounds.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a new paradigm for high-dimensional information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase separation in biomolecular condensates and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can sense, classify, and respond to signals via collective behavior.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable efficient, noise-robust computation in cells, with potential for implementing logic gates and memory.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful framework for cellular information processing, suggesting new directions for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the dynamics of quantum circuits and compute thermalization times.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and have implications for quantum simulation and thermalization.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive measurements and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms without destroying them, and use the same technique to continuously load atoms into arrays. The experiment is performed in finite magnetic fields to control atomic states.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, improving the efficiency and scalability of neutral-atom quantum platforms.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful technique for neutral-atom arrays, enabling new capabilities for quantum information processing with these systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method uses single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from single-shot measurements, demonstrating its effectiveness on a qubit platform.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, which can aid in understanding and mitigating decoherence.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom hardware which has unique constraints.
method: The authors design a transversal logical gate set tailored to neutral-atom hardware, incorporating small-angle rotation error correction and extending it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from quantum information theory, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss function based on circuit expressivity and noise parameters.
result: They find that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a concentration of the loss function that is less severe than in the noiseless case.
conclusion: The results provide a principled way to design noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, guiding experimental implementations.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables multiple logical measurements simultaneously on quantum LDPC codes, leveraging the code's structure to avoid additional overhead.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining key code properties such as distance and locality, without requiring additional code blocks.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Implements noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
