conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for reliable quantum simulations.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: Generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to Majorana-based qubits, designing tailored gates, measurements, and high-rate codes.
motivation: Majorana-based qubits are promising for topological quantum computing but require fault-tolerant protocols adapted to their fermionic nature and constraints.
method: Extends standard qubit error correction techniques to fermionic systems, constructing fault-tolerant operations and codes using Majorana operators and stabilizer formalism.
result: Demonstrates fault-tolerant gates and measurements for Majorana qubits and presents high-rate quantum codes optimized for this platform.
conclusion: Provides a foundation for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana-based qubits, bridging theory and experimental implementation.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian effects are often neglected due to computational complexity; a unified overview of simulation methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various numerical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes and applications.
conclusion: Non-Markovian dynamics can be efficiently simulated using modern methods, enabling accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics, quantum optics, and solid-state physics.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer resource-efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates and simplify algorithm implementations.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and reviews experimental demonstrations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce the number of elementary operations for certain gates and algorithms, with proof-of-principle experiments showing feasibility.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, though challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
authors: Shane Dooley
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians, using factorizability of Pauli strings.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are a mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking; the paper aims to provide a systematic method to realize stabilizer states as scars.
method: The authors define a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings and construct parent Hamiltonians whose ground or excited states are stabilizer states with scar properties.
result: They show that any stabilizer state can be embedded as a QMBS in a local Hamiltonian, and provide explicit examples.
conclusion: This work offers a new perspective on QMBS and may enable controlled studies of ergodicity breaking in many-body systems.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, proposing a framework to quantify how well such states can be told apart.
motivation: Quantum state distinguishability is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing, but non-Gaussian states are less studied than Gaussian ones.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination and information-theoretic measures to analyze distinguishability of non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states become distinguishable and quantify the advantage over Gaussian states.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian states offer enhanced distinguishability, which could benefit quantum technologies, but the work is primarily theoretical and not directly tied to the user's core interests.

title: Universal Composite Phase Gates With Tunable Target Phase
authors: Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, And Andon A. Rangelov
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, and Andon A. Rangelov

We present a systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with a continuously tunable target phase. Using a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of the single-pulse propagator, we design gates from an even number of nominal [MATH] pulses and derive analytic phase families by cance…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with continuously tunable target phase using Cayley-Klein parametrization.
motivation: Composite pulses are essential for high-fidelity quantum control, but existing methods often fix the target phase; a universal gate with tunable phase is needed for flexible quantum operations.
method: The authors use a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of single-pulse propagators and design gates from an even number of nominal π pulses, deriving analytic phase families by canceling errors.
result: They demonstrate universal composite phase gates that can achieve any target phase with high fidelity, robust against pulse area errors.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a versatile tool for quantum control, enabling precise phase manipulation in quantum information processing.

title: Feedback Cooling And Thermometry Of A Single Trapped Ion Using A Knife Edge
authors: Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, and Gerd Leuchs

We report on a simple and easy to implement method of feedback cooling trapped ions to temperatures below those achievable using only Doppler cooling. Additionally, the feedback cooling results in significantly shorter cooling times. For selected parameters, we demonstrate cooling to temperatures be…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063717] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates feedback cooling of a single trapped ion using a knife edge, achieving sub-Doppler temperatures and faster cooling.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but cooling to the motional ground state is essential for high-fidelity operations. This work aims to simplify and improve cooling methods.
method: A knife edge is used to spatially modulate the ion's fluorescence, providing a signal for feedback cooling. The method is implemented on a single trapped ion and compared to standard Doppler cooling.
result: Feedback cooling achieves temperatures below the Doppler limit and significantly reduces cooling time for selected parameters.
conclusion: The knife-edge feedback cooling technique is simple, effective, and can be easily integrated into existing trapped-ion setups, potentially improving quantum gate fidelities.

title: Beyond Trotterization: Variational Product Formulas For Quantum Simulation
authors: Ibsal Assi, Michael Vogl, Meenu Kumari, And J. P. F. Leblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Ibsal Assi, Michael Vogl, Meenu Kumari, and J. P. F. LeBlanc

The authors introduce here a variational splitting scheme for the time-evolution operator that surpasses standard Trotter-Suzuki decompositions. Unlike typical variational methods, this framework works directly in operator space, providing globally valid results irrespective of the targeted initial state. The method generalizes naturally to a wide range of applications in condensed matter physics and beyond. In particular, it enables quantum circuits with lower gate counts and higher accuracy than Trotter-based formulas, making it useful for near-term quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214314] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a variational product formula for quantum simulation that outperforms Trotter-Suzuki decompositions in gate count and accuracy.
motivation: Standard Trotter-Suzuki decompositions for quantum simulation require many gates; variational methods typically depend on initial states. The authors aim to develop a state-independent variational splitting scheme.
method: They propose a variational framework that works directly in operator space, optimizing a cost function to approximate the time-evolution operator without reference to a specific initial state.
result: The variational product formulas achieve lower gate counts and higher accuracy compared to Trotter-based formulas, demonstrated on condensed matter models.
conclusion: The method is useful for near-term quantum computing, enabling more efficient quantum circuits for simulation.

title: Quantum Complexity And Localization In Random And Time-periodic Unitary Circuits
authors: Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, And Pingal Pratyush Nath
abstract:
Author(s): Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, and Pingal Pratyush Nath

We study the growth and saturation of complexity in Krylov basis in random quantum circuits. In Haar-random unitary evolution, we show that, for large system sizes, this notion of complexity grows linearly before saturating at a late-time value of [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hilbert space dimension, at …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214312] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Studies Krylov complexity growth and saturation in random and time-periodic unitary circuits.
motivation: To understand quantum complexity in many-body systems and its relation to localization phenomena.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Krylov basis complexity in Haar-random and Floquet unitary circuits.
result: Complexity grows linearly and saturates at a value proportional to Hilbert space dimension; localization suppresses growth.
conclusion: Krylov complexity provides a useful probe of quantum dynamics and localization in random circuits.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improve VQE performance by using quantum information measures to design efficient ansätze for atomic systems.
method: Starts with an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information metrics to construct a compact ansatz.
result: Demonstrates accurate ground-state energies for atomic systems with fewer parameters than heuristic ansätze.
conclusion: Quantum information-inspired ansätze can enhance VQE efficiency for quantum chemistry on near-term devices.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems by combining real-time evolution with the finite-temperature Lanczos method.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is computationally challenging; classical methods like the finite-temperature Lanczos method are limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses a quantum computer to perform real-time evolution and Lanczos iterations, enabling thermal state preparation and observable estimation.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems, showing accurate thermal averages with polynomial resources, and is expected to scale favorably on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: QFTLM provides a practical quantum algorithm for finite-temperature simulations, potentially outperforming classical methods for certain systems.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems is key to probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom observed; sensitivity achieved that constrains topological entropy isolation.
conclusion: The technique can probe entropy in quantum Hall systems, but does not directly advance quantum thermodynamics or information theory.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high rate and constant-depth encoding, used for magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes enable magic state generation with lower overhead and higher noise thresholds compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient classical simulation method for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and simulating quantum expectation landscapes is important for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to reduce this cost by focusing on local patches.
method: They develop a technique to classically surrogate a small subregion of the expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using polynomial or kernel-based regression.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation of local patches, potentially enabling better understanding of barren plateaus and optimization landscapes in quantum machine learning.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum landscapes, but its contribution is more algorithmic than foundational to quantum information theory.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and Fisher information near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can lead to Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route to surpass classical limits, but practical challenges remain.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to reduce the number of T gates.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces T-count compared to standard methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning method that captures temporal correlations in frequency space for efficient and accurate predictions.
method: They employ Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables and operator growth in Floquet systems, leveraging the frequency-domain structure of periodic driving.
result: The FNO approach accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond training data and generalizes to different driving parameters, demonstrating physically faithful modeling of Floquet Hamiltonians and observable dynamics.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a powerful data-driven tool for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, enabling efficient prediction of long-time dynamics and operator growth.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot properties.
result: These codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: Abelian multi-cycle codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities with improved efficiency.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of large matrices is important for quantum many-body systems, but worst-case complexity is high.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to detect clusters and estimate multiplicities without full diagonalization.
result: The algorithm achieves sub-worst-case complexity for certain spectral properties.
conclusion: Provides a practical quantum algorithm for spectral analysis, though not directly advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties surpass thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur when measurements are made under conditions that break the assumptions of the bounds, such as non-equilibrium or nonlinear regimes.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exploit these assumption violations to achieve properties beyond classical thermodynamic limits, but this does not violate thermodynamics itself.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves force sensitivity below the standard quantum limit by using a levitated nanoparticle.
motivation: Detecting extremely weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter, requires surpassing the zero-point fluctuation limit of mechanical sensors.
method: The authors use optical trapping and feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle, combined with interferometric readout, to resolve forces below the zero-point motion.
result: They demonstrate force sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations, enabling detection of impulses as small as a few yoctonewton-seconds.
conclusion: This work advances nanomechanical sensing into a regime previously inaccessible, with applications in fundamental physics and force microscopy.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods using cold atoms are emerging but limited to cold atoms. This work extends cavity-free control to thermal gases.
method: Exploits collective radiation from a thermal gas to achieve transverse-mode control without a cavity.
result: Demonstrates a new cavity-free method for mode control applicable to thermal gases.
conclusion: Provides a simpler, more accessible approach for controlling light modes, potentially useful for quantum networking or sensing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how environment-induced interactions affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms near a reflecting boundary.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the focus here is on environmental effects rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects.
method: Uses open quantum systems framework with master equations, incorporating atom-boundary and interatomic interactions mediated by the vacuum field.
result: Environment-induced interactions can enhance or suppress entanglement depending on atomic separation and boundary distance.
conclusion: The boundary and interatomic interactions significantly modify entanglement dynamics, but the work is primarily a study of decoherence and entanglement in a specific physical setting.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
authors: Zhiming Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how quantum state texture evolves under Lorentz transformations for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
motivation: To understand the relativistic behavior of a newly proposed quantum resource, quantum state texture, which quantifies global structural complexity.
method: Analytical calculations of QST under Lorentz boosts for single-qubit and two-qubit states, including maximally entangled states.
result: QST is invariant under certain Lorentz transformations for single-particle states but shows competition and sensitivity for bipartite entangled states.
conclusion: Relativistic effects can alter QST, which may have implications for quantum information processing in relativistic settings.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Spin-boson Model With A Continuous Bosonic Spectrum: Exceptional Points And Dynamics
authors: Yong-Xin Zhang And Qing-Hu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Xin Zhang and Qing-Hu Chen

This work studies a [MATH]-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model consisting of a non-Hermitian two-level system coupled to a continuous bosonic bath. The static properties of the system are analyzed through a projection method derived from the displacement operator. We find that only a si…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063723] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model with a continuous bosonic bath, focusing on exceptional points and dynamics.
motivation: To understand the static and dynamic properties of a non-Hermitian quantum system coupled to a continuum, which is relevant for open quantum systems and PT-symmetric physics.
method: A projection method derived from the displacement operator is used to analyze the static properties, and the dynamics are studied via the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
result: Only a single exceptional point is found in the static analysis, and the dynamics show distinct behaviors depending on the system parameters.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric spin-boson model exhibits unique features due to the continuous bosonic spectrum, but the results are primarily of interest to the non-Hermitian quantum physics community.

title: Error Convergence Of Quantum Linear System Solvers
authors: Matias Ginzburg And Ugo Marzolino
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Ginzburg and Ugo Marzolino

The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm remains a paradigmatic quantum routine for solving linear systems and a widely used benchmark in theoretical and experimental studies. Several circuit-level variants have been proposed to simplify its implementation, including constructions in which the cloc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062436] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the error convergence of quantum linear system solvers, focusing on the HHL algorithm and its variants.
motivation: Understanding the error behavior of quantum linear system solvers is important for practical implementation, but the paper does not present novel information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.
method: The authors study the error convergence of HHL-type algorithms, likely through analytical bounds or numerical simulations.
result: The paper provides insights into how errors accumulate and converge in quantum linear system solvers.
conclusion: The work contributes to the analysis of quantum algorithms but is not directly aligned with the user's core research interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, overcoming the usual limitation by the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited in order by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to demonstrate that non-Markovianity can bypass this restriction.
method: They analyze a model of a quantum system coupled to a structured environment with memory effects, using non-Markovian master equations to study the spectral properties.
result: They find that non-Markovian dynamics can produce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order, even in systems with few degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity provides a new mechanism for generating high-order exceptional points, with potential applications in sensing and control of open quantum systems.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
authors: Jaromír Fiurášek
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are important for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; optimizing success probability is crucial.
method: The author uses a theoretical framework based on Gaussian states and photon-counting measurements, deriving upper bounds on heralding probabilities using semidefinite programming and analytical techniques.
result: Maximum heralding probabilities are obtained for various target states, showing trade-offs between state quality and success probability.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits and practical guidelines for generating nonclassical states via heralding, aiding experimental implementations.

title: Spin-correlation Dynamics: A Semiclassical Framework For Nonlinear Quantum Magnetism
authors: Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, And Johan H. Mentink
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, and Johan H. Mentink

Classical nonlinear theories are highly successful in describing far-from-equilibrium dynamics in magnetism, including phenomena such as parametric resonance, ultrafast switching, and even chaos. However, at ultrashort length and time scales, where quantum correlations become significant, these mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214436] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for nonlinear quantum magnetism that captures spin-correlation dynamics beyond classical theories.
motivation: Classical nonlinear theories fail at ultrashort scales where quantum correlations matter; a framework bridging classical and quantum dynamics is needed.
method: The authors develop a semiclassical approach that incorporates quantum correlations into nonlinear spin dynamics, likely using mean-field or truncated Wigner approximations.
result: The framework reproduces classical nonlinear phenomena while capturing quantum effects such as entanglement and squeezing in spin systems.
conclusion: The semiclassical framework provides a practical tool for studying far-from-equilibrium quantum magnetism, but its primary focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics.

title: Exact Nonlinear Dynamics Of Single Band Metallic Systems With Dissipation: From Optical To Dc Currents
authors: J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

The theory of open quantum systems is one of the most essential tools for the development of quantum technologies. A particular area of interest is in the optical response of solid state systems, where dissipation is introduced phenomenologically through the relaxation time approximation and its eff…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224309] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an exact nonlinear response theory for open quantum systems with dissipation, applied to metallic systems for optical and DC currents.
motivation: To provide a rigorous framework for nonlinear optical response in dissipative solid-state systems beyond phenomenological relaxation time approximations.
method: Uses the Keldysh formalism and a master equation approach to derive exact nonlinear conductivities for a single-band metal with dissipation.
result: Obtains closed-form expressions for nonlinear optical and DC currents, showing how dissipation affects nonlinear response and revealing new features beyond the relaxation time approximation.
conclusion: The exact nonlinear theory provides a more accurate description of dissipative quantum systems and can be applied to understand nonlinear transport in metals.

title: Controlled Zeno-induced Localization Of Free Fermions In A Quasiperiodic Chain
authors: Pinaki Singha, Nilanjan Roy, Marcin Szyniszewski, And Auditya Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Pinaki Singha, Nilanjan Roy, Marcin Szyniszewski, and Auditya Sharma

We investigate measurement-induced localization in a continuously monitored one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper model, focusing on the quantum Zeno regime in which the measurements dominate coherent dynamics. The presence of a quasiperiodic potential renders the problem analytically tractable and ena…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235122] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates measurement-induced localization in a quasiperiodic fermionic chain under continuous monitoring, focusing on the quantum Zeno regime.
motivation: To understand how frequent measurements can induce localization in a quasiperiodic system, which is relevant to quantum control and thermodynamics of measurement.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the Aubry-André-Harper model with continuous monitoring, using the quantum Zeno effect to simplify dynamics.
result: Measurements can induce localization even when the quasiperiodic potential is weak, and the localization properties depend on measurement strength and potential parameters.
conclusion: The interplay of quasiperiodicity and measurement-induced Zeno dynamics provides a controllable way to engineer localization, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Pseudospin Formulation Of Quench Dynamics In The Semiclassical Holstein Model
authors: Lingyu Yang, Ho Jang, Sankha Subhra Bakshi, Yang Yang, And Gia-Wei Chern
abstract:
Author(s): Lingyu Yang, Ho Jang, Sankha Subhra Bakshi, Yang Yang, and Gia-Wei Chern

We present a pseudospin formulation for the postquench dynamics of charge-density-wave (CDW) order in the half-filled spinless Holstein model on a square lattice, assuming spatially homogeneous evolution. This Anderson pseudospin description captures the coherent nonequilibrium dynamics of the coupl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A pseudospin formulation is developed to study quench dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the Holstein model, revealing a dynamical transition and prethermalization.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated electron-phonon systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors map the Holstein model to an Anderson pseudospin Hamiltonian and solve the quench dynamics using a self-consistent mean-field approach.
result: They find a dynamical transition between prethermal and thermal regimes, and identify a prethermal plateau in the CDW order parameter.
conclusion: The pseudospin formulation captures key features of the quench dynamics, including prethermalization, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics but the paper focuses on condensed matter rather than thermodynamic bounds.

title: Exact Steady States And Fragmentation-induced Relaxation In The No-passing Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
authors: Urei Miura
abstract:
Author(s): Urei Miura

We introduce a multispecies generalization of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with a “no-passing” constraint, forbidding overtaking, on a one-dimensional reflecting (closed) chain without particle reservoirs. This no-passing rule fragments the Hilbert space into an exponential number of disj…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process with a no-passing constraint, revealing Hilbert space fragmentation and exact steady states.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in constrained classical systems with many degrees of freedom, which may have implications for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors introduce a no-passing rule in a multispecies ASEP on a closed chain, analyze the fragmentation of the Hilbert space, and derive exact steady states using matrix product ansatz or combinatorial methods.
result: The Hilbert space fragments into exponentially many disconnected sectors, each with its own steady state, leading to a relaxation that is not described by a unique stationary distribution.
conclusion: The no-passing constraint causes strong fragmentation, resulting in a rich set of steady states and slow relaxation, relevant for understanding glassy dynamics and ergodicity breaking.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-averaged displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, deriving scaling laws for normal and anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding single-particle tracking dynamics is important for characterizing transport in complex systems, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic processes without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function applicable to both normal and anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing correlated measurements in single-particle tracking, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: Resetting processes are a simple way to generate non-equilibrium steady states, and understanding underdamped dynamics is important for realistic systems where inertia matters.
method: The authors solve the underdamped Langevin equation with Poissonian resetting events, considering two resetting protocols: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while randomizing velocity according to a Maxwell distribution.
result: They derive exact expressions for the stationary probability density functions and other observables, showing that the two protocols lead to different steady-state properties.
conclusion: The work provides a complete analytical treatment of underdamped Brownian motion under resetting, highlighting the role of the resetting protocol in shaping the non-equilibrium steady state.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion in overdamped stochastic systems induce directed motion and negative mobility.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion in stochastic systems without external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion tensor and reflecting boundaries.
result: The no-flux condition at boundaries leads to oblique reflection, creating a drift; negative mobility is observed under certain conditions.
conclusion: Boundary-induced drift is a generic phenomenon in confined anisotropic stochastic systems, with implications for transport in biological and nanoscale systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic approach to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic method successfully captures the anomalous fluctuations in these systems.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: A specular ray-tracing algorithm is employed to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Violation of Kirchhoff's law leads to directional thermal currents and monochromatic heat transfer in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable control over thermal radiation directionality and spectral selectivity, with potential for thermal management applications.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photon pairs where conventional polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles (polarization symmetry) holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for the state to be a Bell state, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, but the application is niche and the contribution is incremental.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, which have no equilibrium counterpart.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven-dissipative system within the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: They identify topological phases and nonreciprocal transport in the open Floquet chain.
conclusion: The work extends topological concepts to open driven systems, but is more focused on condensed matter physics than on information thermodynamics.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand the role of nonstabilizerness, a key resource for quantum computation, in molecular systems and to see if it offers new insights into chemical bonding beyond entanglement.
method: The authors compute magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using ab initio quantum chemistry methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve, indicating that nonstabilizerness captures features of bonding not captured by entanglement alone.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary quantum-information-theoretic insight into molecular bonding, potentially linking quantum resource theory to chemistry.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins at high magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device physics.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic cooling followed by slower nuclear spin-mediated relaxation.
conclusion: The interplay between electrons and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, which has implications for thermal management in quantum devices.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era.
method: The authors use strong and weak symmetry reductions to optimize stabilizer decompositions, enabling tractable simulation of multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the computational cost of simulating Clifford-dominated circuits, extending the reach of classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics (e.g., open systems) on quantum computers requires efficient dilation methods that avoid connectivity bottlenecks.
method: The paper uses a moment-matching technique to construct a unitary dilation on a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling efficient quantum algorithms.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path for simulating linear differential equations and nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work establishes practical measures for Majorana bound state quality, guiding experimental efforts toward realizing topological qubits.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method propagates errors through the circuit to the end, allowing classical simulation of logical magic state preparation protocols with reduced overhead.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating magic state preparation, enabling analysis of larger protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for designing and verifying magic state preparation protocols, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases and optical responses.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and transient orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) in Mott insulators.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: Classical gravity is poorly tested at quantum scales; massive quantum systems may reveal quantum aspects of gravity.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art and outlines future directions for testing gravity with quantum probes.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems are promising interfaces for studying gravity, but no definitive results yet.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models, particularly brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality framework and its relationship to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Optical Tautochrone And Squeezing Dynamics In Nonuniform Lattices
authors: Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, And Konstantinos G. Makris
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, and Konstantinos G. Makris

We present exact analogies between the tautochrone problem of classical mechanics and the squeezed states of quantum optics to optical lattices. Both phenomena emerge in the same physical system, that of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings. Extension to two dimensions yields Lissajous-type tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezing in nonuniform optical lattices, demonstrating exact solutions for waveguide arrays.
motivation: To explore connections between classical mechanics and quantum optics in the context of optical lattices with nonuniform couplings.
method: The authors derive exact analytical solutions for the dynamics of light in waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings, showing that the tautochrone condition leads to squeezing.
result: They find that nonuniform couplings can produce both tautochrone (isochronous) behavior and squeezing dynamics, and extend the concept to two-dimensional Lissajous-type trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework linking classical tautochrone motion and quantum squeezing, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, and is primarily a condensed matter physics result.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional quantum systems beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental realization in a Bose gas, using techniques from quantum field theory and ultracold atom experiments.
result: Identifies fractional Fermi sea behavior in the critical states, revealing new universality classes.
conclusion: The work expands the understanding of quantum criticality in one dimension, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments.
motivation: To demonstrate the application of quantum annealing for computing molecular properties, specifically electric dipole moments.
method: Quantum annealing is used to simulate molecular Hamiltonians; dipole moments are extracted via finite-field method by applying an electric field perturbation.
result: The computed dipole moments for several molecules are presented and compared with classical calculations.
conclusion: Quantum annealing can be a viable tool for molecular property calculations, though accuracy and scalability remain challenges.

title: Stability Of Current-carrying States In Hard-core Bosons With Long-range Hopping On A Square Lattice
authors: Yoshihiro Yabuuchi And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshihiro Yabuuchi and Ippei Danshita

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the stability of superfluid currents in lattice models with long-range hopping is important for condensed matter theory, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to analyze the Bose-Hubbard model with algebraically decaying hopping amplitudes on a square lattice.
result: They find that the stability of current-carrying states depends on the hopping exponent and interaction strength.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of hard-core bosons but does not align with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Photodetection Of Squeezed Light: A Whittaker-Shannon Analysis
authors: Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, And J. E. Sipe
abstract:
Author(s): Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, and J. E. Sipe

The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition provides a temporally localized description of squeezed light, making it applicable in the continuous-wave limit and leading to a definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs at a time. We show examples of its usefulness by calculating quad…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063719] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light in the continuous-wave limit, defining a squeezing strength based on photon pair counts.
motivation: To provide a temporally localized description of squeezed light that is applicable in the continuous-wave limit, improving upon standard frequency-domain approaches.
method: Uses the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to represent squeezed light in the time domain and calculates quadrature variances and photon pair statistics.
result: Derives a new definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs at a time and demonstrates its utility through examples.
conclusion: The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition offers a useful time-domain framework for analyzing squeezed light, with potential applications in quantum optics and metrology.

title: Biorthogonal Scattering And Generalized Unitarity In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, And Hee Chul Park
abstract:
Author(s): Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, and Hee Chul Park

We investigate the two-port scattering process in non-Hermitian dimer models via quantum measurements using external leads. We focus on two exemplary dimer models that preserve parity-time symmetry via spatial gain-loss balance and exhibit nonreciprocity due to directional hopping. The scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062213] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models with parity-time symmetry and nonreciprocity, focusing on biorthogonal scattering and generalized unitarity.
motivation: To understand scattering processes in non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant to open quantum systems and photonics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze two-port scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models using external leads, employing biorthogonal quantum mechanics and scattering matrix formalism.
result: They derive generalized unitarity relations and characterize scattering properties such as transmission and reflection in the presence of gain and loss.
