[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric linearization principle, focusing on anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions observed in complex systems.
method: Introduces a linearization principle at the dynamical level to derive nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric perspective.
result: A geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations is presented, linking the linearization principle to anomalous diffusion.
conclusion: The work offers a new geometric framework for understanding nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations and their role in complex systems.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: Inverse problems in experimental data often require reconstructing probability distributions from limited measurements; information geometry provides a natural framework for such transformations.
method: The authors apply information geometry to define a manifold structure on the space of probability distributions and use geodesic flows or other geometric transformations to map between distributions.
result: The method is demonstrated on synthetic and experimental data, showing improved reconstruction accuracy compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Information geometry offers a principled way to handle distribution transformations for inverse problems, with potential applications in various experimental sciences.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit the effects of time modulation on light propagation in photonic circuits, particularly for frequency conversion and amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis using coupled-mode theory and transfer matrix methods for time-modulated resonant structures.
result: Demonstrates that under certain conditions, time-modulated photonic circuits can achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light frequency with minimal loss.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits offer a new mechanism for frequency conversion and amplification, with potential applications in classical and quantum photonics.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence via a Lyapunov function.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models of associative memory, bridging neuroscience and machine learning.
method: Introduces a coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamical system with a Lyapunov function and entropy-regularized replicator equation for astrocytic gains.
result: The dynamics converge globally to fixed points, and the model exhibits emergent self-attention-like behavior.
conclusion: The model provides a biologically plausible mechanism for attention in associative memory, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method to compute momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for both noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a scalable tool for studying electronic structure in complex moiré materials.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an amplitudelike mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for studying macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying their modes is key to understanding the condensed phase.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitudelike mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the collective excitations of excitonic insulators, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore analogies between classical and quantum critical phenomena.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities such as compressibility and specific heat near the critical endpoint of the Mott transition, comparing them to classical fluid behavior and identifying a line analogous to the Frenkel line.
result: They find that maxima in thermodynamic response functions define a line in the phase diagram of the Hubbard model, similar to the Frenkel line in classical fluids, which separates different dynamical regimes.
conclusion: The analogy between classical and electronic fluids provides a unified perspective on critical phenomena, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of classical configuration interaction methods by leveraging quantum computers to identify the most relevant Slater determinants, reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
method: The algorithm uses a quantum computer to prepare an approximate ground state and then measures in the computational basis to sample important configurations; these configurations are used to construct a reduced Hamiltonian that is diagonalized classically.
result: The method is demonstrated on small molecules and shows that with a modest number of quantum measurements, accurate energies can be obtained, outperforming classical truncated CI methods.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction is a promising hybrid approach for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices, though it requires further validation on larger systems.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules, focusing on radiation pressure forces from two-frequency components.
motivation: Understanding and improving laser cooling and trapping of molecules is important for precision measurements and quantum science, but the paper is primarily an atomic/molecular physics study.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap using two closely spaced frequency components with opposite circular polarization, deriving the radiation pressure force from dark-state effects.
result: They identify that when Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference, a dark state exists for one beam direction, generating a net force toward the field zero, enabling trapping and cooling.
conclusion: The identified mechanism explains how blue-detuned MOTs for molecules can work, providing a basis for experimental implementation.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization approach for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid using field theory techniques.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and their signatures can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and predicts experimental observables, advancing the study of topological excitations in quantum spin chains.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel numerical approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to regularize and numerically simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries like supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superstructures, which are of interest for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling to identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are identified in EuAg4Sb2, demonstrating a design framework for spin moiré superstructures.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin textures in moiré materials, with potential applications in information storage and processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices.
method: The authors perform theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, linking to cryptographic protocols based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can be used as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptography.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic tools.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; existing methods often lack physical grounding.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can significantly improve causal link prediction in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.
method: The authors performed nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements and analyzed critical exponents to identify the universality class of the phase transition.
result: They found evidence of hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state, with the transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the exotic magnetic phases of kagome ice systems and the role of symmetry breaking.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in classical statistical mechanics of fluids.
motivation: To understand the unusual behavior of hyperuniform fluids at the liquid-vapor critical point, where density fluctuations are suppressed yet susceptibility is high.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations but enhanced susceptibility at the critical point, deviating from ordinary fluids.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids present a new class of critical behavior that may have implications for understanding phase transitions in systems with constrained fluctuations.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures, measuring spin-dependent transport.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can support coherent spin manipulation through electron optics, relevant for spintronics.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for novel electronic phases.
method: Combined time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and theoretical modeling to probe excitations across equilibrium and hidden states.
result: Discovery of unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can create long-lived metastable phases with distinct lattice and electronic properties, offering a route to control material functionality.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that achieves exponential speedup over classical methods.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for extracting features from data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that computes persistence diagrams using quantum linear algebra and topological invariants.
result: They prove an exponential quantum speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical applications of topological data analysis that are classically intractable.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between current quantum computing capabilities and real-world applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of the field's progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to demonstrate an end-to-end quantum algorithm that can be executed on near-term devices.
method: The authors design a complete pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, using the Hadamard test and quantum phase estimation to evaluate the Jones polynomial at roots of unity.
result: They implement the algorithm on trapped-ion and superconducting qubit platforms, showing that the algorithm can be run with high fidelity for small knots, and discuss scaling to larger instances.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial algorithm may offer a quantum advantage for certain knot invariants.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To develop a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to represent target states and design a photon catalysis procedure to realize them with a predictable number of steps.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared using realistic experimental tools, with the number of steps determined by the tensor rank.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics and photonic quantum computing.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: Covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on electronic states and many-body phenomena arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the exotic electronic states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands, driven by frustration and interference effects.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated and topological electronic phases, with implications for future quantum materials.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many fields, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The paper tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain an active area with future research opportunities, but the paper is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological features.
result: Highlights key candidate materials and their chiral edge modes, summarizing the current understanding of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising material platforms, but further work is needed to confirm their existence and properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze simultaneous recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for predicting neural activity, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including their formation and quantum features.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering their topological field configurations and quantum interactions.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic applications.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experiments and remaining parameter space.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental improvements and theoretical developments are needed.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of quantum many-body systems in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulating condensed matter and gravitational phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling simulation of topological phases and models of gravity.
method: The paper surveys platforms such as ultracold atoms, photonic systems, and electronic materials, discussing how to engineer fractal lattices, synthetic dimensions, and curved spaces.
result: It summarizes key experimental achievements and theoretical proposals for realizing synthetic quantum matter in these geometries, highlighting connections to topology and cosmology.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to uncover new physics, but it remains largely exploratory and not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Trace Anomaly Of Cold Dense Matter Constrained By Collective Flow
authors: Bao-An Li
abstract:
Author(s): Bao-An Li

The trace anomaly of dense matter, [MATH], defined through the ratio [MATH] of pressure [MATH] to energy density [MATH], quantifies deviations from conformal symmetry and provides a dimensionless measure of the stiffness of the equation of state (EOS) relevant for both neutron stars and hea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 242301] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the trace anomaly of cold dense matter constrained by collective flow in heavy-ion collisions, relevant to neutron star and heavy-ion physics.
motivation: Understanding the equation of state of dense matter is crucial for neutron stars and heavy-ion collisions; the trace anomaly provides a dimensionless measure of stiffness.
method: The author analyzes collective flow data from heavy-ion collisions to constrain the trace anomaly of dense matter.
result: The study yields constraints on the trace anomaly, linking pressure and energy density in dense matter.
conclusion: The trace anomaly is a useful observable for probing the equation of state of dense matter.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of Berry curvature in generating nonlinear Hall effects without external magnetic fields.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 under an in-plane magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
result: A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism involving the Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new nonlinear transport mechanism in topological semimetals, with potential applications in rectification and frequency doubling.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Observation of switchable chiral magnons in altermagnet MnTe via polarized neutron scattering.
motivation: To provide unambiguous evidence of chirality in split magnon bands of altermagnets, a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: Polarized inelastic neutron scattering on MnTe single crystals.
result: First direct observation of chiral magnon bands in an altermagnet.
conclusion: Confirms theoretical predictions of chirality in altermagnets, opening avenues for spintronics.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), enabling production of ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a hydride molecule provides an alternative route.
method: The authors laser-cool and magneto-optically trap calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules using a custom MOT setup, then photodissociate them to produce ultracold hydrogen atoms.
result: Successful trapping of CaH molecules and subsequent generation of ultracold hydrogen atoms with temperatures in the microkelvin range.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable method for producing ultracold atomic hydrogen, opening new possibilities for precision spectroscopy and quantum gas experiments.

title: Role Of Anionic Lone-Pair-Like Electrons In Producing Minimum Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, and Zhigang Zou

Cationic lone-pair electrons are often associated with distinctive phonon properties (e.g., strong lattice anharmonicity) that lead to low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). However, the reliance on specific cations (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) severely restri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236301] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the role of anionic lone-pair-like electrons in achieving minimum lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectric materials.
motivation: To overcome the limitation of relying on specific cations for low lattice thermal conductivity by exploring anionic lone-pair-like electrons.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements to analyze phonon properties and thermal transport.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new strategy for designing materials with minimum lattice thermal conductivity.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action for long time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations require many small time steps to maintain accuracy, which is computationally expensive. The authors aim to reduce the number of steps by learning a surrogate model that can take larger steps.
method: They propose a machine learning approach that learns the action (a time-integrated quantity) of the system, enabling accurate predictions over longer time intervals without simulating every intermediate step.
result: The method achieves accurate long-time-step predictions, significantly reducing computational cost while preserving essential dynamical properties.
conclusion: Learning the action is a promising strategy for accelerating molecular dynamics simulations, with potential applications in materials science and chemistry.

title: High-resolution Spectroscopy Of $^{162}\mathrm{Dy}$ Rydberg Levels
authors: G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, And A. Fioretti
abstract:
Author(s): G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, and A. Fioretti

The authors report on the high-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in
[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062807] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in dysprosium using two-color trap depletion spectroscopy and multichannel quantum defect theory.
motivation: To characterize Rydberg states in dysprosium, which is important for applications in quantum simulation and sensing, but the paper focuses on atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Two-color trap depletion spectroscopy in a magneto-optical trap combined with multichannel quantum defect theory analysis.
result: Measured and assigned over 700 Rydberg states, identified six perturbing states belonging to higher ionization limits.
conclusion: The work provides a benchmark for dysprosium Rydberg states, aiding future experiments in quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Alternative Representation Of Multichannel Rydberg Spectra: A Modified $K$-matrix And Lu-Fano Plot Applied To The Manganese Spectroscopy
authors: Justin D. Piel And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Justin D. Piel and Chris H. Greene

The well-known graphical representation called the Lu-Fano plot was originally developed for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy, especially in quantum-defect theory. The present study shows some of the limitations of this traditional Lu-Fano plot that are desirable to improve on, when there are close…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062805] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a modified K-matrix and Lu-Fano plot for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy in manganese.
motivation: Traditional Lu-Fano plots have limitations when there are close-lying channels; the authors aim to improve the graphical representation for better analysis of Rydberg spectra.
method: The authors develop an alternative representation using a modified K-matrix and a new Lu-Fano plot, applied to manganese spectroscopy data.
result: The modified approach overcomes some limitations of the traditional Lu-Fano plot, providing clearer visualization of multichannel interactions.
conclusion: The new representation is a useful tool for analyzing complex Rydberg spectra, particularly in atoms with many interacting channels.

title: Th:SBO Single Crystal: A Multifunction Material For Solid-state Nuclear Optical Clocks
authors: Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, And Shining Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, and Shining Zhu

The authors grow thorium-doped strontium tetraborate (Th:SBO) single crystals via the Czochralski method and characterize their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties. The Th:SBO crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable a dual-functional platform that integrates nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060801] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the growth and characterization of thorium-doped strontium tetraborate single crystals for potential use in solid-state nuclear optical clocks.
motivation: To develop a dual-functional platform that combines nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host for nuclear optical clock applications.
method: Th:SBO single crystals were grown via the Czochralski method, and their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties were characterized.
result: The crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable integration of nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.
conclusion: Th:SBO is a promising multifunctional material for solid-state nuclear optical clocks.

title: Demonstration Of An Interferometric Technique For Measuring Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence With An Optical Cavity
authors: Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, And Laura Roberts
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, and Laura Roberts

Vacuum magnetic birefringence (VMB) is an effect predicted by quantum electrodynamics in which the vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium and exhibits a birefringence in the presence of a magnetic field. In this work, an interferometric scheme is introduced to measure this effect by sensing th…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063518] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an interferometric technique to measure vacuum magnetic birefringence, a QED effect, using an optical cavity.
motivation: Vacuum magnetic birefringence is a predicted QED effect that has not been directly observed; measuring it would test QED predictions.
method: The authors use an optical cavity to enhance the signal and an interferometric scheme to detect the tiny birefringence induced by a magnetic field.
result: They present a proof-of-principle demonstration of the technique, showing sensitivity sufficient to measure the effect.
conclusion: The technique offers a viable path to directly observe vacuum magnetic birefringence, providing a test of QED.

title: Exciton-induced Frequency Shift In High-harmonic Generation From Solids
authors: Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, And Jian Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, and Jian Wu

Spectroscopy serves as a key experimental pathway for probing many-body dynamics. Among them, high-harmonic generation (HHG) spectroscopy is particularly valued for its subcycle temporal resolution. Recent investigations have confirmed that excitonic effects in crystals can significantly enhance har…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-induced frequency shifts in high-harmonic generation from solids, focusing on many-body effects in strong-field physics.
motivation: To understand how excitonic effects modify high-harmonic generation spectra in solids, which could improve spectroscopic probes of many-body dynamics.
method: The authors theoretically model HHG in solids including exciton interactions, likely using time-dependent density functional theory or semiconductor Bloch equations.
result: Excitonic effects cause a frequency shift in the high-harmonic spectrum, which can be used to extract information about exciton binding energies and dynamics.
conclusion: Exciton-induced frequency shifts provide a new spectroscopic tool for studying excitons in solids with subcycle temporal resolution.

title: Tetrahedral Ferromagnetic Correlations And A Glassy-freezing Anomaly In The Breathing Pyrochlore Magnet ${\mathrm{AgInCr}}_{4}{\mathrm{S}}_{8}$ With Partial $A$-site Disorder
authors: Yuya Haraguchi, Masahiro Kitamura, Masaki Gen, Yusuke Nambu, Akira Matsuo, Koichi Kindo, Masaki Kondo, Masashi Tokunaga, And Hiroko Aruga Katori
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Haraguchi, Masahiro Kitamura, Masaki Gen, Yusuke Nambu, Akira Matsuo, Koichi Kindo, Masaki Kondo, Masashi Tokunaga, and Hiroko Aruga Katori

We investigate the chromium breathing-pyrochlore sulfide [MATH], a chromium-based thiospinel, by synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity. Diffraction confirms the [MATH] breathing structure with alternating lar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations and glassy freezing in a breathing pyrochlore magnet with partial A-site disorder.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of the breathing pyrochlore AgInCr4S8, which exhibits tetrahedral ferromagnetic correlations and a glassy-freezing anomaly.
method: Synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity measurements.
result: Confirmation of breathing structure, observation of ferromagnetic correlations within tetrahedra, and a glassy freezing anomaly at low temperatures.
conclusion: The partial A-site disorder leads to a unique magnetic state with coexisting ferromagnetic and glassy features.

title: Coupling Of Magnetic And Lattice Collective Excitations In The Two-dimensional Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{FePS}}_{3}$
authors: Kartik Panda, Itzik Kapon, Dumitru Dumcenco, Dirk van der Marel, Alexey B. Kuzmenko, And Nimrod Bachar

Author(s): Kartik Panda, Itzik Kapon, Dumitru Dumcenco, Dirk van der Marel, Alexey B. Kuzmenko, and Nimrod Bachar

We combine polarized infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday angle rotation measurements to map the collective excitations of the van der Waals antiferromagnet [MATH]. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), the phonon spectrum becomes …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235124] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coupling between magnetic and lattice collective excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday rotation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between phonons and magnons in two-dimensional magnetic materials, which is important for fundamental physics and potential spintronic applications.
method: Polarized infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday angle rotation measurements were performed on FePS3 below the Néel temperature to map collective excitations.
result: The phonon spectrum shows modifications due to coupling with magnetic excitations, revealing hybridized magnon-phonon modes.
conclusion: The study demonstrates strong magneto-elastic coupling in FePS3, providing insights into the dynamics of 2D antiferromagnets.

title: Observation Of Momentum Dependent Charge Density Wave Gap In ${\mathrm{EuTe}}_{4}$
authors: Iftakhar Bin Elius, Nathan Valadez, Gyanendra Dhakal, Volodymyr Buturlim, Sabin Regmi, Dante James, Peter Radanovich, Keng Tou Chu, Ellis Thompson, Matthew Yankowitz, Tetiana Romanova, Andrzej Ptok, Krzysztof Gofryk, Dariusz Kaczorowski, And Madhab Neupane

Charge density wave (CDW) phenomena in low-dimensional rare-earth chalcogenides have drawn considerable interest owing to their interplay with lattice instabilities, electronic correlations, and magnetism. [MATH], which contains both mono- and bilayer Te pseudosquare nets together wit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235125] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a momentum-dependent charge density wave gap in EuTe4 using ARPES and DFT.
motivation: To understand the interplay between charge density waves, lattice instabilities, and magnetism in rare-earth chalcogenides.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: A momentum-dependent CDW gap is observed, with signatures of strong electron-phonon coupling and possible magnetic interactions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the complex electronic structure of EuTe4 and its potential for studying correlated electron phenomena.

title: Sommerfeld Coefficient Enhancement And Magnetic Short-range Order In A Hyperkagome $3d$ Electron System
authors: Shin-Ichi Shamoto, Yukio Yasui, Kanako Yoshizawa, Yukio Noda, Miwako Takahashi, Yoshichika Ōnuki, Yoshinori Haga, Motoyuki Ishikado, Hiroki Yamauchi, Tsung-Cheng Huang, Min Kai Lee, And Lieh-Jeng Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Shin-ichi Shamoto, Yukio Yasui, Kanako Yoshizawa, Yukio Noda, Miwako Takahashi, Yoshichika Ōnuki, Yoshinori Haga, Motoyuki Ishikado, Hiroki Yamauchi, Tsung-Cheng Huang, Min Kai Lee, and Lieh-Jeng Chang

[MATH]-Mn shows a large Sommerfeld coefficient of 70 mJ [MATH], which is one of the largest values in [MATH]-electron systems. Although the origin has been attributed to the fluctuating magnetic moment, there are no material-dependent systematic studies in the [MATH]-electron…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235126] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Sommerfeld coefficient enhancement and magnetic short-range order in a hyperkagome 3d electron system, focusing on material-specific properties.
motivation: To understand the origin of the large Sommerfeld coefficient in Mn-based hyperkagome systems, which is attributed to fluctuating magnetic moments but lacks systematic study.
method: Experimental measurements including specific heat, magnetic susceptibility, and neutron scattering on hyperkagome materials.
result: Observation of enhanced Sommerfeld coefficient and evidence of magnetic short-range order.
conclusion: The large Sommerfeld coefficient is linked to magnetic fluctuations and short-range order, providing insight into correlated electron systems.

title: Low-energy Excitations In $A$-site Ordered ${\mathrm{SmBaMn}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{6}$
authors: Mirian Garcia Fernandez, Abhishek Nag, Stefano Agrestini, Sahil Tippireddy, Dirk Backes, Xiaoyang Chen, Urs Staub, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Kejin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Mirian Garcia Fernandez, Abhishek Nag, Stefano Agrestini, Sahil Tippireddy, Dirk Backes, Xiaoyang Chen, Urs Staub, Taka-Hisa Arima, and Kejin Zhou

The electron in a solid can be considered a bound state of the three independent, fundamental degrees of freedom creating quasiparticles: spinons, carrying the electron spin; plasmons, carrying the collective charge mode; and orbitons, carrying its orbital degree of freedom. These fundamental degree…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235128] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-energy excitations in A-site ordered SmBaMn2O6, focusing on spin, charge, and orbital degrees of freedom in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin, charge, and orbital excitations in a correlated electron material with A-site ordering.
