authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to probe the percolation of active forces.
result: When active units are too sparse, increasing activity reduces the macroscopic active response, a 'more is less' effect.
conclusion: Percolation of active forces is crucial for macroscopic activity; sparsity can lead to counterintuitive suppression.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond driven by subsurface compliant regions, focusing on mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale.
motivation: Understanding and engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond is important for applications in nanotechnology and materials science.
method: The authors use experimental characterization and possibly simulations to investigate how subsurface structures affect the elastic response of nanodiamond particles of varying sizes.
result: They find that subsurface compliant regions enable an elastic response to strain, leading to size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond.
conclusion: The work provides a method for engineering mechanical properties of diamond, which could have implications for nanodevices and composite materials.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, and Michael J. Shelley

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021009] Published Thu Apr 09, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for chromatin segregation in cell nuclei based on active hydrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces and flows drive spatial organization of euchromatin and heterochromatin in cells.
method: Develops an active hydrodynamic theory modeling chromatin as a two-fluid system with active stresses.
result: The model predicts spontaneous segregation and patterning of chromatin types driven by active forces.
conclusion: Mechanical forces and flows are key to chromatin organization, with implications for gene regulation.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open challenges in accurately modeling internal conversion in complex systems.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to better predict and control internal conversion for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Geometric Bookkeeping Guide To Feynman Integral Reduction And $ϵ$-Factorized Differential Equations
authors: Iris Bree, Federico Gasparotto, Antonela Matijašić, Pouria Mazloumi, Dmytro Melnichenko, Sebastian Pögel, Toni Teschke, Xing Wang, Stefan Weinzierl, Konglong Wu, And Xiaofeng Xu
abstract: Author(s): Iris Bree, Federico Gasparotto, Antonela Matijašić, Pouria Mazloumi, Dmytro Melnichenko, Sebastian Pögel, Toni Teschke, Xing Wang, Stefan Weinzierl, Konglong Wu, and Xiaofeng Xu (
tldr: This paper presents improvements in Feynman integral reduction and epsilon-factorized differential equations for high-energy physics calculations.
motivation: Feynman integral reduction is crucial for multi-loop scattering amplitudes in particle physics, but current methods are computationally intensive.
method: The authors introduce a specific choice of prefactors to trivialize epsilon dependence in integration-by-parts identities and optimize the reduction process.
result: They achieve more efficient reduction and simpler epsilon-factorized differential equations, enabling higher-order calculations.
conclusion: These improvements streamline Feynman integral computations, benefiting precision phenomenology in collider physics.

title: $D$-Meson Production Via Sequential Hadronization In High-Energy Nuclear Collisions
authors: Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Jiaxing Zhao, And Pengfei Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Jiaxing Zhao, and Pengfei Zhuang

Heavy flavor production serves as an ideal probe of the hadronization mechanism of the quark-gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy ion collisions. We study charm-quark hadronization using Langevin transport in the medium together with a sequential coalescence model. Since [MATH] forms earlie…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 232301] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charm-quark hadronization in heavy-ion collisions using a Langevin transport model with sequential coalescence, focusing on D-meson production.
motivation: Heavy flavor production is a probe of the hadronization mechanism of quark-gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
method: The authors use Langevin transport to model charm-quark diffusion in the medium and a sequential coalescence model for hadronization.
result: The model predicts D-meson yields and spectra, showing sensitivity to the hadronization mechanism.
conclusion: Sequential coalescence provides a good description of D-meson production, offering insights into the hadronization process in heavy-ion collisions.

title: Mass Probe Of Tetrahedral Symmetry In Atomic Nuclei
authors: F. F. Xu (许方方) And P. W. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): F. F. Xu (许方方) and P. W. Zhao (赵鹏巍)

Tetrahedral symmetry has long been predicted as an exotic shape degree of freedom in atomic nuclei, yet clear experimental manifestations remain elusive. We show that the triple binding energy difference [MATH] can isolate a structural effect of tetrahedral symmetry in [MATH].…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 232503] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a triple binding energy difference as a probe for tetrahedral symmetry in atomic nuclei.
motivation: Tetrahedral symmetry in atomic nuclei has been predicted but lacks clear experimental evidence; the authors aim to identify a measurable signature.
method: The authors analyze the triple binding energy difference using theoretical nuclear structure calculations.
result: They show that this observable can isolate a structural effect of tetrahedral symmetry.
conclusion: The proposed observable may help detect tetrahedral symmetry in future experiments.

title: Recoil Corrections To Muonic Hydrogen Hyperfine Splitting
authors: Andrzej Maroń, Mateusz Pańtak, And Krzysztof Pachucki
abstract:
Author(s): Andrzej Maroń, Mateusz Pańtak, and Krzysztof Pachucki

This work attempts to present a complete theory of the [MATH] hyperfine splitting, including all contributions above 1 ppm. Quantum electrodynamic and recoil corrections are calculated directly, while the proton structure correction is obtained with the help of the H hyperfine splitting. The …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062810] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates recoil corrections to muonic hydrogen hyperfine splitting using quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: To improve the theoretical prediction of muonic hydrogen hyperfine splitting, which is important for testing bound-state QED and determining fundamental constants.
method: The authors compute quantum electrodynamic and recoil corrections analytically and numerically, incorporating proton structure effects via experimental H hyperfine data.
result: They present a complete theory of the hyperfine splitting including all contributions above 1 ppm.
conclusion: The calculated hyperfine splitting provides a precise theoretical benchmark for future experiments.

title: Hadronic Vacuum Polarization Effect In Muonic Atoms
authors: Zoia A. Mandrykina, Moritz Thierfeld, And Natalia S. Oreshkina
abstract:
Author(s): Zoia A. Mandrykina, Moritz Thierfeld, and Natalia S. Oreshkina

The hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) corrections to energy levels in muonic atoms are studied systematically across the periodic table. Two nuclear charge distribution models have been considered, with a partly analytical solution for a homogeneously charged sphere model and direct numerical integ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062806] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates hadronic vacuum polarization corrections to energy levels in muonic atoms using two nuclear charge distribution models.
motivation: Precision spectroscopy of muonic atoms requires accurate QED corrections, including hadronic vacuum polarization, to test fundamental physics.
method: The authors use a homogeneously charged sphere model with partly analytical solutions and a Fermi distribution model with direct numerical integration to compute HVP contributions.
result: Systematic HVP corrections are presented across the periodic table, showing dependence on nuclear charge distribution.
conclusion: The results improve theoretical predictions for muonic atom energy levels, aiding future precision experiments.

title: Effects Of Screening And Pressure Ionization On The Electron Broadening Of Spectral Lines In Dense Plasmas
authors: J. P. Kinney, S. B. Hansen, T. A. Gomez, And S. D. Baalrud
abstract:
Author(s): J. P. Kinney, S. B. Hansen, T. A. Gomez, and S. D. Baalrud

Collisions between electrons and radiating atoms broaden spectral absorption and emission lines in dense plasmas. High densities also introduce screening and pressure ionization effects that distort the wave functions of both bound and free electrons. In order to study how dense plasma effects influ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062804] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron broadening of spectral lines in dense plasmas, focusing on screening and pressure ionization effects.
motivation: Understanding spectral line shapes in dense plasmas is important for diagnosing plasma conditions in astrophysical and laboratory settings.
method: The authors model collisions between electrons and radiating atoms, incorporating screening and pressure ionization to modify bound and free electron wave functions.
result: They find that dense plasma effects significantly alter line broadening compared to standard models.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of dense plasma effects is necessary for interpreting spectra from high-density plasmas.

title: Lead Transition Metal Oxides: Globally Alike, Locally Very Diverse
authors: A. Bussmann-Holder, A. M. Glazer, A. Majchrowski, I. Lazar, A. Soszyński, And K. Roleder
abstract:
Author(s): A. Bussmann-Holder, A. M. Glazer, A. Majchrowski, I. Lazar, A. Soszyński, and K. Roleder

The lead transition metal oxides [MATH], and [MATH] are shown to be extremely similar in their overall properties, such as soft-mode behavior, phase transitions, and long-wavelength related characteristics. However, locally, they develop very dif…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214106] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the global and local properties of lead transition metal oxides, focusing on soft-mode behavior and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand why lead transition metal oxides exhibit similar global properties but diverse local structures.
method: Experimental characterization and comparison of structural and dynamical properties of PbTiO3, PbZrO3, and related compounds.
result: The materials show nearly identical soft-mode behavior and phase transitions globally, but develop very different local structures.
conclusion: The local diversity arises from subtle differences in bonding and disorder, which are not captured by average structure measurements.

title: Ultrahigh-pressure Structural Evolution Of Holmium To 327 GPa
authors: Hongkai Li, Mingyu Li, Xiaokuan Hao, Zhongyan Wu, Hechong Wang, Shaojie Wang, Jing Song, Ke Yang, Guoying Gao, Lin Wang, And Yongjun Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkai Li, Mingyu Li, Xiaokuan Hao, Zhongyan Wu, Hechong Wang, Shaojie Wang, Jing Song, Ke Yang, Guoying Gao, Lin Wang, and Yongjun Tian

Synchrotron X-ray diffraction measurements of holmium were conducted up to 327 GPa using toroidal diamond-anvil cells, revealing a complete structural sequence of [MATH]. The [MATH] transition initiates around 257 GPa, approximately 60 …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214107] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the structural evolution of holmium under ultrahigh pressure using synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase transitions of rare-earth elements under extreme pressure is important for condensed matter physics and geophysics.
method: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction measurements were performed on holmium samples in toroidal diamond-anvil cells up to 327 GPa.
result: A complete structural sequence was observed, with a transition starting around 257 GPa.
conclusion: The study provides new data on the high-pressure behavior of holmium, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Contrasting Field-driven Behaviors Of Incommensurate And Commensurate Antiferromagnetic Phases In Al/Ga-doped MnNiGe Alloys
authors: Riya Roy, Sanat Kumar Adhikari, Rosni Roy, Jhuma Sannigrahi, Dmitry Khalyavin, Devashibhai T. Adroja, Rajib Mondal, And Souvik Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Roy, Sanat Kumar Adhikari, Rosni Roy, Jhuma Sannigrahi, Dmitry Khalyavin, Devashibhai T. Adroja, Rajib Mondal, and Souvik Chatterjee

The Ge-site-doped MnNiGe alloys with nominal compositions [MATH] and [MATH] are investigated through neutron powder diffraction studies in the presence of external magnetic fields ([MATH]). The application of external [MATH] i…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224426] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies field-driven behaviors of antiferromagnetic phases in doped MnNiGe alloys using neutron diffraction.
motivation: To understand the contrasting responses of incommensurate and commensurate antiferromagnetic phases to external magnetic fields in MnNiGe alloys.
method: Neutron powder diffraction measurements under applied magnetic fields up to 10 T on Al/Ga-doped MnNiGe samples.
result: The incommensurate and commensurate phases exhibit different field-driven behaviors, with the incommensurate phase showing a metamagnetic transition.
conclusion: The study reveals distinct magnetic phase stability and transitions, relevant for understanding magnetostructural coupling in these alloys.

title: Characterizing Emergent Multiscale Dynamics In Colloidal Nanoparticle Gels
authors: William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, And Delia J. Milliron
abstract:
Author(s): William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, and Delia J. Milliron

Characterizing the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks demands a spatiotemporal resolution that no single technique can provide. This Perspective describes the opportunities to address this challenge using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources combined with complementary experimental and simulation tools. This should move the field beyond descriptive fundamental studies toward mechanistic understanding and design of nanoparticle gels with adaptive and programmable behaviors.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 061001] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This perspective discusses characterizing multiscale dynamics in colloidal nanoparticle gels using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy and complementary methods.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks is challenging due to the need for spatiotemporal resolution beyond any single technique.
method: The authors propose combining X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources with complementary experimental and simulation tools.
result: The approach aims to move from descriptive studies to mechanistic understanding and design of adaptive nanoparticle gels.
conclusion: Integrating advanced X-ray techniques with simulations can enable rational design of programmable nanoparticle gels.

title: General Approach For Partitioning And Phase Separation In Macromolecular Coexisting Phases
authors: Vikki Anand Varma And Alberto Scacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Vikki Anand Varma and Alberto Scacchi

Partitioning of (bio)materials in polymeric mixtures is a key phenomenon both in cellular environments, as well as in industrial applications. In cells, macromolecules are distributed among distinct biomolecular phases. The coexistence of polymeric aqueous phases in multicomponent systems has been w…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065414] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies partitioning and phase separation in macromolecular coexisting phases, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how biomaterials partition among distinct phases is important for cellular biology and industrial applications.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical approach based on polymer physics to describe partitioning in multicomponent polymeric mixtures.
result: They derive conditions for phase coexistence and partitioning behavior, validated by comparison with known experimental systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified description of partitioning in macromolecular phases, applicable to both biological and synthetic systems.

title: Global Buckley-Leverett Theory For Multicomponent Flow In Fractured Media: Isothermal Equation-of-state Coupling And Dynamic Capillarity
authors: Christian Tantardini And Fernando Alonso-Marroquín
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Tantardini and Fernando Alonso-Marroquín

We present an isothermal global Buckley-Leverett framework for multicomponent, multiphase flow in porous and fractured media that retains the interpretability of classical Buckley-Leverett while incorporating essential physics: equation-of-state-based phase behavior, multicomponent Maxwell-Stefan di…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065106] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Buckley-Leverett theory to multicomponent, multiphase flow in fractured media with equation-of-state coupling and dynamic capillarity.
motivation: Classical Buckley-Leverett theory is limited to two-phase flow and does not account for multicomponent phase behavior or dynamic capillarity, which are important for realistic reservoir simulation.
method: The authors develop a global framework that integrates equation-of-state-based phase behavior, multicomponent Maxwell-Stefan diffusion, and dynamic capillarity into the Buckley-Leverett formulation.
result: The framework retains the interpretability of classical Buckley-Leverett while incorporating essential physics for multicomponent flow in fractured media.
conclusion: The proposed theory provides a more accurate and interpretable model for multicomponent flow in porous and fractured media, with potential applications in reservoir engineering.

title: Statistical Analysis Of Mass-spectrometry-based Secondary-ion Counting Data: Characterization Of Nanoscale Ultrafast Secondary-ion Emission Phenomena Triggered By Energetic Large-cluster Impacts On Solids
authors: K. Hirata And D. Asakawa
abstract:
Author(s): K. Hirata and D. Asakawa

The complex and interrelated ultrafast phenomena of intense secondary-ion (SI) emission triggered by nanoscale energy deposition by energetic impacts of large-cluster ions of buckminsterfullerene ([MATH]) on solid targets are characterized through a statistical analysis of their mass-an…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065504] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Statistical analysis of secondary-ion emission data from large-cluster impacts on solids, focusing on nanoscale ultrafast phenomena.
motivation: To characterize complex secondary-ion emission processes triggered by energetic cluster impacts, which are important for mass spectrometry and surface analysis.
method: Statistical analysis of mass-spectrometry-based secondary-ion counting data, including modeling of emission statistics and correlation with impact parameters.
result: Identified statistical signatures of nanoscale ultrafast emission phenomena, providing insights into the dynamics of cluster-induced desorption/ionization.
conclusion: The statistical approach effectively reveals underlying physical processes in secondary-ion emission, aiding in the interpretation of mass spectra.

title: Electron Heat Flux And Whistler Instability In The Earth's Magnetosheath
authors: Ida Svenningsson, Emiliya Yordanova, Yuri V. Khotyaintsev, Mats André, Giulia Cozzani, Alexandros Chasapis, And Steven J. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Ida Svenningsson, Emiliya Yordanova, Yuri V. Khotyaintsev, Mats André, Giulia Cozzani, Alexandros Chasapis, and Steven J. Schwartz

Despite heat flux's role in regulating energy conversion in collisionless plasmas, its properties and evolution in the magnetosheath downstream of the Earth's bow shock are scarcely explored. We use Magnetospheric Multiscale in situ measurements to quantify and characterize the electron heat flux in…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L063201] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron heat flux and whistler instability in Earth's magnetosheath using in situ spacecraft measurements.
motivation: Heat flux regulates energy conversion in collisionless plasmas, but its properties in the magnetosheath are poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission data to quantify electron heat flux and its relation to whistler waves.
result: They characterize the electron heat flux and identify conditions for whistler instability in the magnetosheath.
conclusion: The findings improve understanding of energy transport in space plasmas, but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vector Resonant Relaxation And Statistical Closure Theory. Ii. One-loop Closure
authors: Sofia Flores And Jean-Baptiste Fouvry
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Flores and Jean-Baptiste Fouvry

The dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole can be used as a test case for statistical closure schemes that allow the calculation of dynamical correlation functions in the fully nonlinear and nonperturbative regime. The authors develop an iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism, and find that it compares well with numerical simulations.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064127] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a statistical closure scheme for stellar dynamics around a supermassive black hole using the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole and test statistical closure schemes in the nonlinear regime.
method: An iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism is developed and compared with numerical simulations.
result: The iterative scheme compares well with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed closure scheme is effective for calculating dynamical correlation functions in stellar dynamics.

title: Nonequilibrium Assembly Mechanisms Of Janus-polymer-grafted Carbon Nanotubes During Surface-initiated Polymerization-coupled Assembly
authors: Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, and Hong Liu

Surface-initiated polymerization on anisotropic templates provides a useful framework for exploring polymerization-driven self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions. Here, we investigate surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly on idealized Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotube (CNT) tem…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065411] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium assembly of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly.
motivation: To understand how polymerization-driven self-assembly on anisotropic templates can produce complex structures under nonequilibrium conditions.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations to model the surface-initiated polymerization on Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes and observe the assembly dynamics.
result: They identify distinct assembly mechanisms and morphologies depending on grafting density and polymerization rate.
conclusion: The work provides insights into designing nonequilibrium assembly processes for functional nanomaterials.

title: Feasibility And Single Parameter Scaling Of Extinctions In Large Ecological Communities
authors: Philippe Jacquod
abstract:
Author(s): Philippe Jacquod

Multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations exhibit stationary population abundances, where a large number of species often coexist. Understanding the precise conditions under which this is at all feasible and what triggers species extinctions is a key, outstanding proble…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062202] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies species extinctions in large ecological communities using generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
motivation: Understanding the conditions for species coexistence and the triggers of extinctions is a key problem in ecology.
method: The authors analyze stationary population abundances in multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
result: They identify a single parameter scaling that governs extinctions and assess feasibility of coexistence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stability and extinction dynamics of large ecological communities.

title: Edwards Thermodynamic Framework Controls Density Segregation In Cyclically Sheared Granular Materials
authors: Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, And Yujie Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, and Yujie Wang

Granular segregation is a widespread phenomenon observed in various industrial applications, geophysical processes, and daily life events. It can be driven by multiple mechanisms, and numerous models have been proposed to elucidate this behavior. However, most of these models are phenomenological an…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065407] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies density segregation in cyclically sheared granular materials using Edwards' thermodynamic framework.
motivation: Granular segregation is common in industry and nature, but existing models are mostly phenomenological; a thermodynamic approach may provide a unified understanding.
method: The authors apply Edwards' statistical mechanics of granular matter to model density segregation under cyclic shear, likely using simulations or experiments.
result: The Edwards framework successfully predicts segregation patterns, showing that density differences drive segregation analogous to phase separation.
conclusion: Edwards' thermodynamics offers a predictive, first-principles description of granular segregation, bridging granular physics and statistical mechanics.

title: Electron Penetration Heating In Turbulent Magnetic Loops Driven By Nonrelativistic Laser-plasma Interaction
authors: Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, And Matthew R. Edwards
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, and Matthew R. Edwards

Using particle-in-cell simulations to study nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in an under-critical plasma, we identify a novel mechanism that occurs during the growth of turbulent magnetic loops: electron penetration heating. The loops have an electromagnetic left-hand chirality distinct from …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065205] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron penetration heating in turbulent magnetic loops driven by nonrelativistic laser-plasma interaction using particle-in-cell simulations.
motivation: To understand a novel heating mechanism in laser-plasma interactions relevant to laboratory astrophysics and inertial confinement fusion.
method: Particle-in-cell simulations of nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in under-critical plasma.
result: Identified electron penetration heating during growth of turbulent magnetic loops with left-hand chirality.
conclusion: The mechanism may impact energy transport in magnetized plasmas.

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, and M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under averaging.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of adsorbate phases on metal surfaces is important for surface science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) to observe the surface structure and dynamics, combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They find that above the stability temperature, the ordered phase breaks into fluctuating domains that, when averaged, appear to have a different periodicity, leading to a misinterpretation of the surface symmetry.
conclusion: Care must be taken in interpreting averaged surface measurements, as dynamic fluctuations can create false symmetry signals.

title: Revealing Charge Anisotropies In Metal Compounds Via High-purity X-ray Polarimetry
authors: Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, And Ralf Röhlsberger
abstract:
Author(s): Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, and Ralf Röhlsberger

Linear polarization analysis of hard x-rays is employed to probe electronic anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity. We use polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of [MATH] to determine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023297] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses high-purity X-ray polarimetry to probe charge anisotropies in metal compounds via nuclear forward scattering.
motivation: Understanding electronic anisotropies in metal complexes is important for materials science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors employ polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of 57Fe to measure linear polarization of hard X-rays.
result: The technique reveals charge anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity.
conclusion: High-purity X-ray polarimetry is a powerful tool for probing electronic structure, but the work is purely in condensed matter characterization without quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.

title: Commissioning And Full Realization Of A Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Setup At Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility
authors: W. C. Mei et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): W. C. Mei et al.

A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facilit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023286] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper describes the commissioning of a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup for exotic nuclei at a radioactive ion-beam facility.
motivation: To enable precision laser spectroscopy of short-lived isotopes for nuclear structure studies.
method: A PLASEN system combining a radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher with collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy was installed and tested with radioactive beams.
result: The setup was successfully commissioned, demonstrating its capability for high-resolution spectroscopy of exotic nuclei.
conclusion: The system is now operational and will be used for nuclear physics experiments.

title: Excitation Of Confined Bulk Plasmons In Metallic Nanoparticles By Penetrating Electron Beams Within A Nonlocal Analytical Approach
authors: Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, And Nerea Zabala
abstract:
Author(s): Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, and Nerea Zabala

Using a linear hydrodynamic model, we theoretically investigate the interaction between penetrating electron beams and sub-5-nm metallic spherical nanoparticles. We derive an analytical expression of the electron energy loss probability that includes nonlocal effects in the response of the confined …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023279] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron energy loss in metallic nanoparticles using a nonlocal hydrodynamic model, focusing on plasmon excitation.
motivation: To understand nonlocal effects in the optical response of sub-5-nm metallic nanoparticles when probed by penetrating electron beams.
method: A linear hydrodynamic model is used to derive an analytical expression for the electron energy loss probability, incorporating nonlocal dielectric response.
result: The analytical expression reveals how nonlocal effects modify the energy loss spectrum compared to local approximations.
conclusion: Nonlocal effects are significant for small nanoparticles and must be included for accurate interpretation of electron energy loss spectroscopy.

title: Membrane-associated Self-assembly For Cellular Decision-making
authors: Samuel L. Foley And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel L. Foley and Margaret E. Johnson

Cellular decision-making based on information received from the external environment is frequently initiated by transmembrane receptors. These receptors are known to propagate such information by triggering a series of irreversible, energy-consuming reactions. While this active mechanism ensures swi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023280] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies membrane-associated self-assembly for cellular decision-making, a topic in biophysics and systems biology.
motivation: Understanding how cells process external signals to make decisions is fundamental to biology and medicine.
method: The authors use computational modeling and simulations to study self-assembly of membrane-bound proteins.
result: They show that self-assembly can act as a switch for cellular decisions, with timescales and thresholds tunable by parameters.
conclusion: Membrane self-assembly provides a robust mechanism for cellular decision-making without active energy consumption.

title: Visualizing Bulk Band Structure In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{4}\mathrm{N}$ Thin Films By Spin- And Angle-resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy
authors: Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, And Akio Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, and Akio Kimura

The bulk band structure of an in situ prepared ferromagnetic [MATH] thin film has been investigated using spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation. It was observed that most of the bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin. The exper…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023257] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to visualize the bulk band structure of ferromagnetic Fe4N thin films.
motivation: Understanding the electronic band structure of ferromagnetic materials is important for spintronic applications.
method: Spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation was performed on in situ prepared Fe4N thin films.
result: Most bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin, and the experimental band structure agrees well with first-principles calculations.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insight into the spin-dependent electronic structure of Fe4N, relevant for spintronics.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work links microscopic ion motion to macroscopic properties, aiding material design.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.
motivation: Understanding the vibrational properties of glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal behavior, but the connection between stability and low-frequency vibrations is not well understood.
method: The authors use an improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure the vibrational density of states in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: They find that more stable glasses exhibit suppressed low-frequency vibrational modes, indicating a correlation between stability and the boson peak.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the microscopic origin of the boson peak and the role of glass stability in determining vibrational properties.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A multi-step model involving surface defects, electrical stress, heating, and particle emission explains the onset of vacuum arcs.
conclusion: Insights from this work can help design more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on classical wave-matter interactions.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and applications in nuclear energy.
motivation: Transplutonium materials are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique behavior at the boundary of localization and itinerancy.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure, addressing challenges due to radioactivity and complex electronic structure.
result: The review summarizes the current understanding of pressure-induced changes in electronic structure, bonding, and phase transitions in transplutonium materials.
conclusion: The work expands knowledge of heavy-element behavior under extreme conditions, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with implications for nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It highlights the potential of multimessenger observations to understand dense environments in neutron stars.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will provide new insights into neutron star physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial tests of nuclear physics under extreme conditions.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from gravitational-wave signals (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and are compared to extrapolations of nuclear equation of state models.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the interdisciplinary nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No new scientific results; a retrospective on the development of neural networks and physics.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can inspire discoveries across disciplines.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning.
motivation: To present the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of artificial neural networks and their impact on physics and computer science.
method: The lecture reviews the history, theory, and applications of Boltzmann machines, including their connection to statistical physics.
result: Boltzmann machines are a class of stochastic neural networks that can learn complex probability distributions, serving as a precursor to modern deep learning.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have had a profound influence on machine learning and illustrate the cross-fertilization between physics and computer science.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The review highlights capabilities and limitations of each technique and cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, which is essential for understanding material properties.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly due to low rates.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions on Earth.
result: Summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory and outlines new ideas for laboratory measurements.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical effects dominate low-energy stellar reactions, and continued theoretical and experimental efforts are needed to improve our understanding.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology.
method: A least-squares adjustment of all available experimental and theoretical data up to the end of 2022.
result: A self-consistent set of values and conversion factors for physics and chemistry.
conclusion: The CODATA 2022 values provide the most accurate and reliable set of fundamental constants to date.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep tissues with optical contrast.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed to provide biological and clinical insight into cells and tissues, and optoacoustic imaging offers noninvasive deep-tissue imaging with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, where short laser pulses are absorbed by tissues, causing a temperature rise that generates ultrasound waves detected by external sensors.
result: The technique enables imaging of optical contrast at depths of millimeters to centimeters with high resolution, and recent developments combine optical and optoacoustic methods for multimodal microscopy.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical research, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of kinetic solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the origin, stability, and dynamics of isolated potential structures observed in space plasmas.
method: Review of satellite observations, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetically unstable velocity distributions and are stable over long times.
conclusion: These structures are ubiquitous in space plasmas and play a key role in plasma turbulence and transport.

title: Duality Between Correlation Functions And Wilson Loops In Gauge Theory From Effective Field Theory
authors: Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, And Hua Xing Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, and Hua Xing Zhu

In this Letter, we initiate a systematic study of the [MATH]-point correlation functions (CFs) in gauge theories in the sequential light-cone (SLC) limit. Focusing on QCD, we formulate a factorization theorem for the CF of four vector currents in this limit using tools from soft-collinear effective fie…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241601] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies correlation functions and Wilson loops in gauge theories using effective field theory, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the structure of correlation functions in gauge theories in the sequential light-cone limit and their relation to Wilson loops.
method: Uses soft-collinear effective field theory (SCET) to derive a factorization theorem for four-point correlation functions in QCD.
result: Establishes a duality between correlation functions and Wilson loops in the sequential light-cone limit.
conclusion: The factorization theorem provides a systematic framework for studying multi-point correlation functions in gauge theories.

title: Energy Distribution Of The Galactic Center Excess’s Sources
authors: Florian List, Yujin Park, Nicholas L. Rodd, Eve Schoen, And Florian Wolf
abstract:
Author(s): Florian List, Yujin Park, Nicholas L. Rodd, Eve Schoen, and Florian Wolf

The Galactic Center Excess (GCE) may yet herald the discovery of annihilating dark matter. Weighing against that conclusion are analyses showing evidence for dim point sources within the spatial structure of the emission. Because of technical limitations these analyses are purely spatial with all sp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231001] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energy distribution of sources contributing to the Galactic Center Excess, a dark matter or astrophysical phenomenon, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The Galactic Center Excess may be due to annihilating dark matter or unresolved point sources; distinguishing these scenarios is important for astrophysics.
method: The authors perform a combined spatial and energy-based analysis of gamma-ray data from the Galactic Center, using statistical techniques to characterize the energy distribution of the emission.
result: They find evidence that the energy distribution of the GCE is consistent with a population of dim point sources rather than smooth dark matter annihilation.
conclusion: The results favor an astrophysical origin for the GCE over a dark matter interpretation, but further observations are needed to confirm.

title: Primordial-Black-Hole-Based Pathways To Little Red Dots
authors: Valerio de Luca, Loris Del Grosso, Gabriele Franciolini, Konstantinos Kritos, Emanuele Berti, Daniel J. D’orazio, And Joseph Silk
abstract:
Author(s): Valerio De Luca, Loris Del Grosso, Gabriele Franciolini, Konstantinos Kritos, Emanuele Berti, Daniel J. D’Orazio, and Joseph Silk

The James Webb Space Telescope has uncovered a population of compact, high-redshift sources, the Little Red Dots (LRDs), which may host supermassive black holes (BHs) significantly heavier than their stellar content compared with local scaling relations. These objects challenge standard models of ea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231402] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes that primordial black holes could explain the overmassive black holes observed in high-redshift Little Red Dots by JWST.
motivation: JWST discovered compact galaxies with supermassive black holes that are too heavy relative to their stellar mass, challenging standard formation models.
method: The authors model the formation and growth of primordial black holes in the early universe and compare with LRD observations.
result: Primordial black hole seeds can naturally produce the observed black hole masses without requiring super-Eddington accretion.
conclusion: Primordial black holes offer a viable pathway to explain the LRD population, linking them to early universe cosmology.

title: Search For Feebly Interacting Particles In $b$ Decays With Missing Energy At Belle
authors: M. Abumusabh et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Abumusabh et al. (The Belle and Belle II Collaborations)

We present a search for an invisible hidden-sector particle [MATH], produced in [MATH] and [MATH] decays, where [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH]. The search is performed using [MATH] collision data…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231802] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A search for feebly interacting particles in B meson decays with missing energy at the Belle experiment.
motivation: To probe hidden-sector particles that interact weakly with Standard Model particles, motivated by dark matter and new physics.
method: Analysis of electron-positron collision data from Belle, looking for B decays to a kaon and missing energy, with a kinematic fit to isolate signal.
result: No significant excess observed; upper limits set on branching fractions for invisible particle production.
conclusion: The search constrains the parameter space for feebly interacting particles, but no discovery is made.

title: First Measurement Of Time-Dependent $cp$ Violation In The Flavor-Changing Neutral-Current Decay ${B}^{0}→{K}_{S}^{0}{μ}^{+}{μ}^{−}$
authors: R. Aaij et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): R. Aaij et al. (LHCb Collaboration)

The decay of a P violation.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231904] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of time-dependent CP violation in the decay B0 → K0S μ+ μ- by the LHCb collaboration.
motivation: To test the Standard Model prediction of CP violation in flavor-changing neutral-current decays, which are sensitive to new physics.
method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data at the LHC, reconstructing B0 mesons and measuring the time-dependent CP asymmetry.
result: First observation of time-dependent CP violation in this decay mode, with a significance of 5.4 standard deviations.
conclusion: The result is consistent with Standard Model expectations and provides new constraints on beyond-Standard-Model physics.

title: Precise Measurement Of The Chromoelectric Dipole Moment Of The Charm Quark
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
