title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response
authors: Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, And Antoine Allard
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, and Antoine Allard

The unicellular microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CR) is well known for its biflagellated swimming in response to light stimuli. This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to characterize photophobic response.
motivation: Understanding how microalgae coordinate flagella after light stimuli is important for biophysics and cellular behavior.
method: The authors use time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella from high-speed video microscopy.
result: They quantify resynchronization dynamics after a photoshock, revealing characteristic timescales and phase relationships.
conclusion: The method provides a robust way to study flagellar coordination and its response to environmental cues.

title: Controlled Interference Of Laser-induced Shock Waves In Microdroplet Jetting
authors: R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, And O. O. Versolato
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, and O. O. Versolato

We report the formation of high-velocity microjets driven by the interference of two laser-induced shock waves in a tin microdroplet. A first 0.4-ns laser pulse launches a shock wave into the droplet (diameter [MATH], 50, and [MATH]). Due to the droplet's s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies laser-induced shock waves in tin microdroplets to produce high-velocity microjets, with applications in extreme ultraviolet lithography.
motivation: Understanding and controlling microdroplet jetting is important for improving the efficiency of extreme ultraviolet light sources used in semiconductor manufacturing.
method: Two laser pulses are used to create interfering shock waves inside a tin microdroplet, and the resulting jet dynamics are observed with high-speed imaging.
result: The interference of shock waves can be tuned to control the direction and velocity of the ejected microjet.
conclusion: Controlled interference of laser-induced shock waves offers a method to steer microjets, which may enhance the performance of laser-produced plasma sources.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto De Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, and Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distribution from achiral molecules, a phenomenon in photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules is important for interpreting photoemission experiments and for potential applications in molecular imaging.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements using circularly polarized light and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with theoretical modeling based on one-step photoemission theory.
result: They show that circular dichroism can arise purely from the experimental geometry and the molecular orbital symmetry, even in the absence of molecular chirality.
conclusion: The observed circular dichroism is a geometric effect rather than an intrinsic property of the molecule, which must be accounted for in photoemission studies of chiral systems.

title: Sea-surface Retention Effect Shapes Ocean Microplastic Fibers
authors: Andrea Mazzino And Giuseppe Suaria
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Mazzino and Giuseppe Suaria

Microfibers contaminate the global ocean, but their impact depends on length-dependent residence at the air-sea interface. In the submillimeter range, the sea surface exhibits a surface-enrichment signature: The long-to-short fiber ratio is higher at the interface than a few meters below (about 5 m)…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023283] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the length-dependent retention of microplastic fibers at the sea surface, finding that longer fibers are enriched at the air-sea interface compared to subsurface waters.
motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the sea surface are poorly understood, which affects their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of turbulent transport and buoyancy.
result: They observe a higher ratio of long to short fibers at the surface than at depth, indicating a surface-enrichment effect that depends on fiber length.
conclusion: The sea surface selectively retains longer microfibers, which has implications for their transport, degradation, and ecological effects.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Dephasing Reduction In An Optically Guided Laser-plasma Accelerator
authors: Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, And Cédric Thaury
abstract:
Author(s): Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, and Cédric Thaury

Laser-plasma accelerators offer a compact means of producing high-energy electron beams, but their performance is fundamentally limited by dephasing between the accelerated electrons and the plasma wave. To overcome this limitation, we investigate the combination of plasma density tapering and optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023274] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dephasing reduction in a laser-plasma accelerator using plasma density tapering and optical guiding.
motivation: Laser-plasma accelerators are limited by dephasing between electrons and the plasma wave; the authors aim to overcome this to improve electron beam energy and quality.
method: They combine plasma density tapering with optical guiding in a laser-plasma accelerator experiment.
result: The dephasing is reduced, leading to higher energy electron beams.
conclusion: The technique effectively mitigates dephasing, advancing compact accelerator performance.

title: Generation Of Attosecond Pulses From Relativistic Oscillating Plasma Gratings
authors: Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, And Min Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, and Min Chen

We propose a scheme to generate two isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles through the interaction between relativistic laser pulses and a solid target. Two [MATH]-polarized laser pulses with certain frequency chirps are employed to drive oscillating plasma gratings (OPGs) on the target surf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023261] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate attosecond pulses using relativistic oscillating plasma gratings driven by chirped laser pulses.
motivation: Attosecond pulse generation is important for ultrafast science, and the authors aim to produce isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles.
method: Two chirped, p-polarized relativistic laser pulses interact with a solid target to create oscillating plasma gratings, which reflect the pulses into attosecond bursts.
result: The scheme yields two isolated attosecond pulses with controllable emission angles and durations.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a new way to generate attosecond pulses with angular control, potentially useful for pump-probe experiments.

title: Unified Model For Full-stage Shear Thickening Via Surface Chemistry And Friction
authors: Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, And Xinglong Gong
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, and Xinglong Gong

Shear thickening fluid exhibits complex properties in a wide range of external conditions, leading to the significance for probing its state-transition property at the molecular level. Here, we propose a constitutive model that unifies the three rheological stages of shear thinning, shear thickening…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023263] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constitutive model for shear thickening fluids, unifying three rheological stages via surface chemistry and friction.
motivation: Shear thickening fluids exhibit complex state transitions under varying external conditions, and understanding these at the molecular level is important for applications.
method: The authors develop a constitutive model that incorporates surface chemistry and friction effects to describe shear thinning, shear thickening, and the transition between them.
result: The model successfully unifies the three rheological stages and matches experimental data.
conclusion: The unified model provides a molecular-level understanding of shear thickening behavior, which could aid in designing smart materials.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces 'super-resonance' to overcome the bandwidth limit of resonant modes and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a narrow bandwidth, limiting its application in flow control and other areas; the authors aim to achieve broadband out-of-phase response.
method: The authors propose a super-resonance mechanism that maintains a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications.
conclusion: Super-resonance breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, offering new possibilities for flow control and potentially other fields.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]
authors: Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on low-temperature ion-molecule reaction rates, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K; the erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely corrects experimental or theoretical details from the original study.
result: The erratum provides corrected data or interpretations for the D2+ + NH3/ND3 reactions.
conclusion: The correction does not alter the broader field of quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated, resembling the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new path for materials design by linking mechanical deformation to quantum mechanical formalism.
conclusion: The work offers a novel approach to metamaterial design but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is important for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and relate it to bulk hydrogel behavior through a force-response model.
result: They identify how protein unfolding and refolding cycles contribute to fatigue fracture and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for tougher soft materials.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is used to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The vapor training process improves plasticity and enables better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The method offers a way to enhance the mechanical properties of wood-derived films.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial tissues, which are relevant to developmental biology and disease.
method: A three-dimensional bubbly vertex model is developed to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: Cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion, with curvature playing a key role.
conclusion: The model provides insights into how tissue geometry and mechanics influence cell behavior, with implications for morphogenesis and cancer.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the hydrodynamics of microbial motility is important for biology and microfluidics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors used experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming microalga.
result: They discovered unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena that expand understanding of microhydrodynamics.
conclusion: The findings have biological implications for microbial motility and physiology but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, and Huaizhou Zhao

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free approach to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials can convert waste heat into electricity, but traditional doping methods have limitations. A doping-free route is attractive for developing efficient waste heat recovery technologies.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, and characterize the resulting thermoelectric properties.
result: The self-doping approach significantly boosts the thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb.
conclusion: Phase-transition-induced self-doping is an effective strategy to enhance thermoelectric performance without external dopants.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: To understand strong interaction (QCD) by studying charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights recent advances from BESIII as the leading facility.
conclusion: Hadron spectroscopy in charm meson pairs provides crucial insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to multiple scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial compilation of three colloquia, each focusing on a different aspect of Arecibo's scientific achievements.
result: The editorial highlights Arecibo's revolutionary contributions to planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a profound and lasting impact on these fields, and its legacy continues to inspire future research.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of planetary radar observations at Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To summarize the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system after its upgrade.
method: Review of radar techniques and key observations of planets, moons, and asteroids.
result: Highlights unique subsurface and surface insights from radar data that complemented in situ missions.
conclusion: Arecibo radar was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary science, and its loss leaves a gap.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and review of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Summarizes major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities enabled groundbreaking discoveries across astronomy and atmospheric science.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, optical, and satellite instruments.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are highlighted.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory provided unique capabilities for geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform current studies.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the precipitation bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos would enable multimessenger studies.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest theoretical predictions for gravitational wave signatures from neutrino-driven core collapse supernovae.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential of multimessenger observations to probe the supernova central engine and the physics of neutron star formation.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and the ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the cosmic microwave background with that in the distribution of radio galaxies and quasars.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole anisotropy and compare it with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further investigation of systematic effects is needed.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observable effects on galaxy and large-scale structure dynamics.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test beyond-standard-model scenarios where dark matter particles self-interact, which can affect halo formation and evolution.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical predictions of self-interacting dark matter with observational data from galaxies, clusters, and large-scale structure, comparing simulations and analytic models.
result: The paper summarizes current constraints on self-interaction cross-sections and discusses how future observations can distinguish between different dark matter models.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable alternative to cold dark matter, and upcoming astrophysical surveys will provide more stringent tests.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard-Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a survey of remaining viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The review surveys experimental constraints from LHC searches and theoretical developments, and projects discovery potential across multiple search channels for various supersymmetric scenarios.
result: The paper provides an overview of the current status of supersymmetry and projections for the HL-LHC, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain scenarios, and the HL-LHC will have significant discovery potential, but no specific new findings are reported.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and their astrophysical implications.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It summarizes advances in the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning and how diagnostics like solar neutrinos and helioseismology test solar models.
conclusion: The review consolidates current understanding of solar fusion, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Gas bubbles are important in many natural and industrial processes, but their dynamics are complex due to deformability and interactions.
method: The paper reviews recent advances in experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, including effects of turbulence, rheology, and surfactants.
result: Key advances over the past 20 years are summarized, highlighting the influence of liquid properties and flow conditions on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, focusing on collective motion in biological and soft matter systems.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment of active units with their velocity leads to novel collective behaviors, with applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment in active matter, presenting a unified mathematical framework.
result: Self-alignment enables phenomena such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, distinct from neighbor-based alignment.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter that can transform collective motion and has potential for real-world applications.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. [Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: To understand the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth, which is relevant to materials science and biology.
method: Integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: Provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and the nonlinear phenomena accompanying buckling.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity theory is essential for a complete understanding of creases and cusps in growing soft matter.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of gravitational wave signals from the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can probe the first second after the Big Bang, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave production from cosmological phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe sources, along with detection strategies.
result: Summarizes possible gravitational wave signatures and outlines detection methods for stochastic backgrounds.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, but detection requires future observatories.
